[p23.b1] Safety instructions 19
[p23.b2] 1
[p23.b3] Safety instructions
[p23.b4] Contents of this chapter
[p23.b5] This chapter contains the safety instructions which you must obey when you install, start-up, operate and do maintenance work on the drive. If you ignore the safety instructions, injury, death or damage can occur.
[p23.b6] Use of warnings and notes
[p23.b7] Warnings tell you about conditions which can cause injury or death, or damage to the equipment. They also tell you how to prevent the danger. Notes draw attention to a particular condition or fact, or give information on a subject.
[p23.b8] The manual uses these warning symbols:
[p23.b9] WARNING! Electricity warning tells about hazards from electricity which can cause injury or death, or damage to the equipment.
[p23.b10] WARNING! General warning tells about conditions other than those caused by electricity, which can cause injury or death, or damage to the equipment.
[p23.b11] WARNING! Electrostatic sensitive devices warning tells you about the risk of electrostatic discharge which can cause damage to the equipment.
=== page 24 ===
[p24.b1] 20 Safety instructions
[p24.b2] General safety in installation, start-up and maintenance
[p24.b3] These instructions are for all personnel who do work on the drive.
[p24.b4] WARNING! Obey these instructions. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur.
[p24.b5] • Keep the drive in its package until you install it. After unpacking, protect the drive from dust, debris and moisture.
[p24.b6] • Use the required personal protective equipment: safety shoes with metal toe cap, safety glasses, protective gloves and long sleeves, etc. Some parts have sharp edges.
[p24.b7] • Lift a heavy drive with a lifting device. Use the designated lifting points. See the dimension drawings.
[p24.b8] • Be careful when handling a tall module. The module overturns easily because it is heavy and has a high center of gravity. Whenever possible, secure the module with chains. Do not leave an unsupported module unattended especially on a sloping floor.
[p24.b9] • Beware of hot surfaces. Some parts, such as heatsinks of power semiconductors, and brake resistors, remain hot for a while after disconnection of the electrical supply.
[p24.b10] • Vacuum clean the area around the drive before the start-up to prevent the drive cooling fan from drawing the dust inside the drive.
[p24.b11] • Make sure that debris from drilling, cutting and grinding does not enter the drive during the installation. Electrically conductive debris inside the drive may cause damage or malfunction.
[p24.b12] • Make sure that there is sufficient cooling. See the technical data.
[p24.b13] • Before you connect voltage to the drive, make sure that all covers are in place. Do not remove the covers when voltage is connected.
=== page 25 ===
[p25.b1] Safety instructions 21
[p25.b2] • Before you adjust the drive operation limits, make sure that the motor and all driven equipment can operate throughout the set operation limits.
[p25.b3] • Before you activate the automatic fault reset or automatic restart functions of the drive control program, make sure that no dangerous situations can occur. These functions reset the drive automatically and continue operation after a fault or supply break. If these functions are activated, the installation must be clearly marked as defined in IEC/EN/UL 61800-5-1, subclause 6.5.3, for example, "THIS MACHINE STARTS AUTOMATICALLY".
[p25.b4] • The maximum drive power cycles is five times in ten minutes. Power cycling the drive too often can damage the charging circuit of the DC capacitors.
[p25.b5] • If you have connected safety circuits to the drive (for example, Safe torque off or emergency stop), validate them at start-up. See separate instructions for the safety circuits.
[p25.b6] • Beware of hot air exiting from the air outlets.
[p25.b7] • Do not cover the air inlet or outlet when the drive is running.
[p25.b8] Note:
[p25.b9] • If you select an external source for the start command and it is on, the drive will start immediately after fault reset unless you configure the drive for pulse start. See the firmware manual.
[p25.b10] • If the drive is in remote control mode, you cannot stop or start the drive with the control panel.
[p25.b11] • Only authorized persons are allowed to repair a malfunctioning drive.
=== page 26 ===
[p26.b1] 22 Safety instructions
[p26.b2] Electrical safety in installation, start-up and maintenance
[p26.b3] ￭Electrical safety precautions
[p26.b4] These electrical safety precautions are for all personnel who do work on the drive, motor cable or motor.
[p26.b5] WARNING! Obey these instructions. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur.
[p26.b6] If you are not a qualified electrical professional, do not do installation or maintenance work.
[p26.b7] Go through these steps before you begin any installation or maintenance work.
[p26.b8] (step 1) 1. Clearly identify the work location and equipment.
[p26.b9] (step 2) 2. Disconnect all possible voltage sources. Make sure that re-connection is not possible. Lock out and tag out.
[p26.b10] • Open the main disconnecting device of the drive.
[p26.b11] • If you have a permanent magnet motor connected to the drive, disconnect the motor from the drive with a safety switch or by other means.
[p26.b12] • Disconnect all dangerous external voltages from the control circuits.
[p26.b13] • After you disconnect power from the drive, always wait 5 minutes to let the intermediate circuit capacitors discharge before you continue.
[p26.b14] (step 3) 3. Protect any other energized parts in the work location against contact.
[p26.b15] (step 4) 4. Take special precautions when close to bare conductors.
[p26.b16] (step 5) 5. Measure that the installation is de-energized. Use a quality voltage tester.
[p26.b17] • Before and after measuring the installation, verify the operation of the voltage tester on a known voltage source.
[p26.b18] • Make sure that the voltage between the drive input power terminals (L1, L2, L3) and the grounding (PE) busbar is zero.
[p26.b19] • Make sure that the voltage between the drive output terminals (T1/U, T2/V, T3/W) and the grounding (PE) busbar is zero.
[p26.b20] • Make sure that the voltage between the drive DC terminals (UDC+ and UDC-) and the grounding (PE) terminal is zero.
[p26.b21] Note: If cables are not connected to the drive DC terminals, measuring the voltage from the DC terminal screws can give incorrect results.
=== page 27 ===
[p27.b1] Safety instructions 23
[p27.b2] (step 6) 6. Install temporary grounding as required by the local regulations.
[p27.b3] (step 7) 7. Ask for a permit to work from the person in control of the electrical installation work.
[p27.b4] ￭Additional instructions and notes
[p27.b5] WARNING! Obey these instructions. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur.
[p27.b6] If you are not a qualified electrical professional, do not do installation or maintenance work.
[p27.b7] • Make sure that the electrical power network, motor/generator, and environmental conditions agree with the drive data.
[p27.b8] • Do not do insulation or voltage withstand tests on the drive.
[p27.b9] • If you have a cardiac pacemaker or other electronic medical device, keep away from the area near motor, drive, and the drive power cabling when the drive is in operation. There are electromagnetic fields present which can interfere with the function of such devices. This can cause a health hazard.
[p27.b10] Note:
[p27.b11] • When the drive is connected to the input power, the motor cable terminals and the DC bus are at a dangerous voltage. The brake circuit, including the brake chopper and brake resistor (if installed) are also at a dangerous voltage. After disconnecting the drive from the input power, these remain at a dangerous voltage until the intermediate circuit capacitors have discharged.
[p27.b12] • External wiring can supply dangerous voltages to the relay outputs of the control units of the drive.
[p27.b13] • The Safe torque off function does not remove the voltage from the main and auxiliary circuits. The function is not effective against deliberate sabotage or misuse.
[p27.b14] Printed circuit boards
[p27.b15] WARNING! Use a grounding wristband when you handle printed circuit boards. Do not touch the boards unnecessarily. The boards contain components sensitive to electrostatic discharge.
=== page 28 ===
[p28.b1] 24 Safety instructions
[p28.b2] ￭Grounding
[p28.b3] These instructions are for all personnel who are responsible for the grounding of the drive.
[p28.b4] WARNING! Obey these instructions. If you ignore them, injury or death, or equipment malfunction can occur, and electromagnetic interference can increase.
[p28.b5] If you are not a qualified electrical professional, do not do grounding work.
[p28.b6] • Always ground the drive, the motor and adjoining equipment. This is necessary for the personnel safety.
[p28.b7] • Make sure that the conductivity of the protective earth (PE) conductors is sufficient and that other requirements are met. See the electrical planning instructions of the drive. Obey the applicable national and local regulations.
[p28.b8] • When using shielded cables, make a 360° grounding of the cable shields at the cable entries to reduce electromagnetic emission and interference.
[p28.b9] • In a multiple-drive installation, connect each drive separately to the protective earth (PE) busbar of the power supply.
=== page 29 ===
[p29.b1] Safety instructions 25
[p29.b2] General safety in operation
[p29.b3] These instructions are for all personnel that operate the drive.
[p29.b4] WARNING! Obey these instructions. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur.
[p29.b5] • If you have a cardiac pacemaker or other electronic medical device, keep away from the area near motor, drive, and the drive power cabling when the drive is in operation. There are electromagnetic fields present which can interfere with the function of such devices. This can cause a health hazard.
[p29.b6] • Give a stop command to the drive before you reset a fault. If you have an external source for the start command and the start is on, the drive will start immediately after the fault reset, unless you configure the drive for pulse start. See the firmware manual.
[p29.b7] • Before you activate the automatic fault reset or automatic restart functions of the drive control program, make sure that no dangerous situations can occur. These functions reset the drive automatically and continue operation after a fault or supply break. If these functions are activated, the installation must be clearly marked as defined in IEC/EN/UL 61800-5-1, subclause 6.5.3, for example, "THIS MACHINE STARTS AUTOMATICALLY".
[p29.b8] Note:
[p29.b9] • The maximum drive power cycles is five times in ten minutes. Power cycling the drive too often can damage the charging circuit of the DC capacitors. If you need to start or stop the drive, use the control panel keys or commands through the I/O terminals of the drive.
[p29.b10] • If the drive is in remote control mode, you cannot stop or start the drive with the control panel.
[p29.b11] Additional instructions for permanent magnet motor drives
[p29.b12] ￭Safety in installation, start-up, maintenance
[p29.b13] These are additional warnings concerning permanent magnet motor drives. The other safety instructions in this chapter are also valid.
[p29.b14] WARNING! Obey these instructions. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur.
[p29.b15] If you are not a qualified electrical professional, do not do installation or maintenance work.
=== page 30 ===
[p30.b1] 26 Safety instructions
[p30.b2] • Do not do work on the drive when a rotating permanent magnet motor is connected to it. A rotating permanent magnet motor energizes the drive including its input and output power terminals.
[p30.b3] Before installation, start-up and maintenance work on the drive:
[p30.b4] • Stop the drive.
[p30.b5] • Disconnect the motor from the drive with a safety switch or by other means.
[p30.b6] • If you cannot disconnect the motor, make sure that the motor cannot rotate during work. Make sure that no other system, like hydraulic crawling drives, can rotate the motor directly or through any mechanical connection like felt, nip, rope, etc.
[p30.b7] • Do the steps in section Electrical safety precautions (page 22).
[p30.b8] • Install temporary grounding to the drive output terminals (T1/U, T2/V, T3/W). Connect the output terminals together as well as to the PE.
[p30.b9] During the start-up:
[p30.b10] • Make sure that the motor cannot run overspeed, for example, driven by the load. Motor overspeed causes overvoltage that can damage or destroy the capacitors in the intermediate circuit of the drive.
[p30.b11] ￭Safety in operation
[p30.b12] WARNING! Make sure that the motor cannot run overspeed, for example, driven by the load. Motor overspeed causes overvoltage that can damage or destroy the capacitors in the intermediate circuit of the drive.
=== page 31 ===
[p31.b1] Introduction to the manual 27
[p31.b2] 2
[p31.b3] Introduction to the manual
[p31.b4] Contents of this chapter
[p31.b5] This chapter describes the intended audience and contents of the manual. It contains a flowchart of steps in examining the delivery, installing and commissioning the drive. The flowchart refers to chapters/sections in this manual and other manuals.
[p31.b6] Applicability
[p31.b7] This manual applies to the ACS580-01 drives.
[p31.b8] Target audience
[p31.b9] This manual is intended for people who plan the installation, install, commission and do maintenance work on the drive, or create instructions for the end user of the drive concerning the installation and maintenance of the drive.
[p31.b10] Read the manual before working on the drive. You are expected to know the fundamentals of electricity, wiring, electrical components and electrical schematic symbols.
[p31.b11] Categorization by frame size
[p31.b12] The ACS580-01 is manufactured in frames (frame sizes) R1…R9. Some instructions and other information that concern only certain frames are marked with the symbol of the frame (R1…R9). The frame is marked on the type designation label of the drive, see Type designation label (page 46).

=== page 38 ===
[p38.b1] 34 Operation principle and hardware description
[p38.b2] Operation principle
[p38.b3] The ACS580-01 is a drive for controlling asynchronous AC induction motors, permanent magnet motors and synchronous reluctance motors (SynRM).
[p38.b4] The figure below shows the simplified main circuit diagram of the drive.
[p38.t1.r1] column 1: A 1 2 3 L1 T1/U L2 T2/V L3 T3/W 4 5 R- UDC+ UDC- R+
[p38.t1.r2] column 1: A | column 2: Drive
[p38.t1.r3] column 1: 1 | column 2: Rectifier. Converts alternating current and voltage to direct current and voltage.
[p38.t1.r4] column 1: 2 | column 2: DC link. DC circuit between rectifier and inverter.
[p38.t1.r5] column 1: 3 | column 2: Inverter. Converts direct current and voltage to alternating current and voltage.
[p38.t1.r6] column 1: 4 | column 2: Built-in brake chopper (R-, R+) in frames R1…R3. Conducts the surplus energy from the intermediate DC circuit of the drive to the brake resistor when necessary. The chopper operates when the DC link voltage exceeds a certain maximum limit. The voltage rise is typically caused by deceleration (braking) of a high inertia motor. The user obtains and installs the brake resistor when needed.
[p38.t1.r7] column 1: 5 | column 2: DC connection (UDC+, UDC-), for an external brake chopper in frames R4…R9.
[p38.b5] L2 L3
[p38.b6] T2/V T3/W
[p38.b7] Drive A
[p38.b8] Rectifier. Converts alternating current and voltage to direct current and voltage. 1
[p38.b9] DC link. DC circuit between rectifier and inverter. 2
[p38.b10] Inverter. Converts direct current and voltage to alternating current and voltage. 3
[p38.b11] DC connection (UDC+, UDC-), for an external brake chopper in frames R4…R9. 5
[p38.b12] Layout
[p38.b13] Frames R1…R2
[p38.b14] The layout of a frame R1 drive is presented below. The main structure of frame R2 is similar to R1. IP55 / UL Type 12 frames are also slightly different from IP21 / UL Type 1 frames, for example, IP21 / UL Type 1 front cover has two parts while IP55 / UL Type 12 front cover only has one part.

[p52.b2] Type designation key
[p52.b3] The type designation contains information on the specifications and configuration of the drive. You find the type designation on the type designation label attached to the drive. The first digits from the left express the basic configuration, for example, ACS580-01-12A7-4. The optional selections are given after that, separated by plus signs, for example, +L501. The main selections are described below. Not all selections are available for all types.

=== page 55 ===
[p55.b1] Mechanical installation 51
[p55.b2] 4
[p55.b3] Mechanical installation
[p55.b4] Contents of this chapter
[p55.b5] This chapter tells how to examine the installation site, unpack and examine the delivery and install the drive mechanically.
[p55.b6] Safety
[p55.b7] WARNING! Frames R5…R9: Lift the drive with a lifting device. Use the lifting eyes of the drive. Do not tilt the drive. The drive is heavy and its center of gravity is high. An overturning drive can cause physical injury.
=== page 56 ===
[p56.b1] 52 Mechanical installation
[p56.b2] Examining the installation site
[p56.b3] The drive must be installed on the wall or an enclosure. There are three alternative ways to install it:
[p56.b4] • Vertical
[p56.b5] Note: Do not install the drive upside down.

=== page 61 ===
[p61.b1] Mechanical installation 57
[p61.b2] Make sure that the installation site complies with the requirements below:
[p61.b3] • The installation site is sufficiently ventilated or cooled to remove the heat away from the drive. See Losses, cooling data and noise (page 273).
[p61.b4] • The operation conditions of the drive meet the specifications given in Ambient conditions (page 300).
[p61.b5] • The wall is as close to vertical as possible, of non-flammable material and strong enough to carry the weight of the drive, see Dimensions, weights and free space requirements (page 265).
[p61.b6] • The floor/material below the installation is non-flammable.
[p61.b7] • There is enough free space above and below the drive to enable cooling air flow, service and maintenance. See the required free space tables for each of the different mounting alignments on page 52 (or page 265).
[p61.b8] Required tools
[p61.b9] To install the drive mechanically, you need the following tools:
[p61.b10] • drill with suitable bits
[p61.b11] • screwdriver set (Torx, flat and/or Phillips, as appropriate)
[p61.b12] • socket set (metric)
[p61.b13] • tape measure, if you will not be using the provided mounting template.
[p61.b14] Moving the drive
[p61.b15] Frames R5…R9: Move the transport package by pallet truck to the installation site.

[p78.b1] 74 Mechanical installation
[p78.b2] Installing the drive
[p78.b3] ￭Installing the drive vertically, frames R1…R4
[p78.b4] The figures show frame R3 as an example.
[p78.b5] Select fasteners and their application to meet local requirements appropriate to wall surface materials, drive weight and application.
[p78.b6] (step 1) 1. Mark the hole locations using the mounting template included in the package. Do not leave the mounting template under the drive. The drive dimensions and hole locations are also shown in the drawings in chapter Dimension drawings (page 309).
[p78.b7] (step 2) 2. Drill the mounting holes.
[p78.b8] (step 3) 3. Insert anchors or plugs into the holes and start the bolts into the anchors or plugs.

[p89.b1] Guidelines for planning the electrical installation 85
[p89.b2] 5
[p89.b3] Guidelines for planning the electrical installation
[p89.b4] Contents of this chapter
[p89.b5] This chapter contains guidelines for planning the electrical installation of the drive.
[p89.b6] Limitation of liability
[p89.b7] The installation must always be designed and made according to applicable local laws and regulations. ABB does not assume any liability whatsoever for any installation which breaches the local laws and/or other regulations. Furthermore, if the recommendations given by ABB are not followed, the drive may experience problems that the warranty does not cover.
[p89.b8] Selecting the main supply disconnecting device
[p89.b9] You must equip the drive with a main supply disconnecting device which meets the local safety regulations. You must be able to lock the disconnecting device to the open position for installation and maintenance work.
=== page 90 ===
[p90.b1] 86 Guidelines for planning the electrical installation
[p90.b2] ￭European Union and United Kingdom
[p90.b3] To meet the European Union Directives and United Kingdom Regulations, according to standard EN 60204-1, Safety of Machinery, the disconnecting device must be one of the following types:
[p90.b4] • switch-disconnector of utilization category AC-23B (IEC 60947-3)
[p90.b5] • disconnector that has an auxiliary contact that in all cases causes switching devices to break the load circuit before the opening of the main contacts of the disconnector (EN 60947-3)
[p90.b6] • circuit-breaker suitable for isolation in accordance with IEC 60947-2.
[p90.b7] ￭North America
[p90.b8] Installations must be compliant with NFPA 70 (NEC)1) and/or Canadian Electrical Code (CE) along with state and local codes for your location and application.
[p90.b9] (step 1) 1) National Fire Protection Association 70 (National Electric Code).
[p90.b10] ￭Other regions
[p90.b11] The disconnecting device must conform to the applicable local safety regulations.
[p90.b12] Examining the compatibility of the motor and drive
[p90.b13] Use asynchronous AC induction motors, permanent magnet synchronous motors or ABB synchronous reluctance motors (SynRM motors) with the drive.
[p90.b14] Select the motor size and drive type from the rating table on basis of the AC line voltage and motor load. You can find the rating table in the appropriate hardware manual. You can also use the DriveSize PC tool.
[p90.b15] Make sure that the motor can be used with an AC drive. See Requirements table (page 87). For basics of protecting the motor insulation and bearings in drive systems, see Protecting the motor insulation and bearings (page 86).
[p90.b16] Note:
[p90.b17] • Consult the motor manufacturer before using a motor with nominal voltage that differs from the AC line voltage connected to the drive input.
[p90.b18] • The voltage peaks at the motor terminals are relative to the supply voltage of the drive, not to the drive output voltage.
[p90.b19] ￭Protecting the motor insulation and bearings
[p90.b20] The drive employs modern IGBT inverter technology. Regardless of frequency, the drive output comprises pulses of approximately the drive DC bus voltage with a very short rise time. The pulse voltage can almost double at the motor terminals, depending on
=== page 91 ===
[p91.b1] Guidelines for planning the electrical installation 87 [p91.b2] the attenuation and reflection properties of the motor cable and the terminals. This can cause additional stress on the motor and motor cable insulation.
[p91.b3] Modern variable speed drives with their fast rising voltage pulses and high switching frequencies can generate current pulses that flow through the motor bearings. This can gradually erode the bearing races and rolling elements.
[p91.b4] du/dt filters protect motor insulation system and reduce bearing currents. Common mode filters mainly reduce bearing currents. Insulated N-end (non-drive end) bearings protect the motor bearings.
[p91.b5] ￭Requirements table
[p91.b6] These tables show how to select the motor insulation system and when a drive du/dt and common mode filters and insulated N-end (non-drive end) motor bearings are required. Ignoring the requirements or improper installation may shorten motor life or damage the motor bearings and voids the warranty.

[p94.b13] Additional requirements for explosion-safe (EX) motors
[p94.b14] If you use an explosion-safe (EX) motor, follow the rules in the requirements table above. In addition, consult the motor manufacturer for any further requirements.
[p94.b15] Additional requirements for ABB motors of types other than M2_, M3_, M4_, HX_ and AM_
[p94.b16] Use the selection criteria given for non-ABB motors.
[p94.b17] Additional requirements for braking applications
[p94.b18] When the motor brakes the machinery, the intermediate circuit DC voltage of the drive increases, the effect being similar to the motor supply voltage increasing by up to 20 percent. Consider this voltage increase when specifying the motor insulation requirements if the motor will be braking a large part of its operation time.
[p94.b19] Example: Motor insulation requirement for a 400 V AC line voltage application must be selected as if the drive were supplied with 480 V.
[p94.b20] Additional requirements for the regenerative and low harmonics drives
[p94.b21] It is possible to increase the intermediate circuit DC voltage from the nominal (standard) level with a parameter in the control program. If you choose to do this, select the motor insulation system which withstands the increased DC voltage level.
[p94.b22] Additional requirements for ABB high-output and IP23 motors
[p94.b23] The rated output power of high output motors is higher than what is stated for the particular frame size in EN 50347 (2001).

[p98.b1] 94 Guidelines for planning the electrical installation
[p98.b2] Selecting the power cables
[p98.b3] ￭General guidelines
[p98.b4] Select the input power and motor cables according to local regulations.
[p98.b5] • Current: Select a cable capable of carrying the maximum load current and suitable for the prospective short-circuit provided by the supply network. The method of installation and ambient temperature affect the cable current carrying capacity. Obey local regulations and laws.
[p98.b6] • Temperature: For an IEC installation, select a cable rated for at least 70 °C (158 °F) maximum permissible temperature of conductor in continuous use. For North America, select a cable rated for at least 75 °C (167 °F). Important: For certain product types or option configurations higher temperature rating may be required. See the technical data for details.
[p98.b7] • Voltage: 600 V AC cable is accepted for up to 500 V AC. 750 V AC cable is accepted for up to 600 V AC. 1000 V AC cable is accepted for up to 690 V AC.
[p98.b8] To comply with the EMC requirements of the CE mark, use one of the preferred cable types. See Preferred power cable types (page 94).
[p98.b9] Symmetrical shielded cable reduces electromagnetic emission of the whole drive system as well as the stress on motor insulation, bearing currents and wear.
[p98.b10] Metal conduit reduces electromagnetic emission of the whole drive system.
[p98.b11] ￭Typical power cable sizes
[p98.b12] See the technical data.
[p98.b13] ￭Power cable types
[p98.b14] Preferred power cable types
[p98.b15] This section presents the preferred cable types. Make sure that the selected cable type also complies with local/state/country electrical codes.

[p100.b6] (step 1) 1) Armor may act as an EMC shield, as long as it provides the same performance as a concentric EMC shield of a shielded cable. To be effective at high frequencies, the shield conductivity must be at least 1/10 of the phase conductor conductivity. The effectiveness of the shield can be evaluated based on the shield inductance, which must be low and only slightly dependent on frequency. The requirements are easily met with a copper or aluminum shield/armor. The cross-section of a steel shield must be ample and the shield helix must have a low gradient. A galvanized steel shield has a better high-frequency conductivity than a non-galvanized steel shield.

[p102.b3] ￭Power cable shield
[p102.b4] If the cable shield is used as the sole protective earth (PE) conductor, make sure that its conductivity agrees with the PE conductor requirements.
[p102.b5] To effectively suppress radiated and conducted radio-frequency emissions, the cable shield conductivity must be at least 1/10 of the phase conductor conductivity. The requirements are easily met with a copper or aluminum shield. The minimum requirement of the motor cable shield of the drive is shown below. It consists of a concentric layer of copper wires with an open helix of copper tape or copper wire. The better and tighter the shield, the lower the emission level and bearing currents.

[p102.b12] Grounding requirements
[p102.b13] This section gives general requirements for grounding the drive. When you plan the grounding of the drive, obey all the applicable national and local regulations.
[p102.b14] The conductivity of the protective earth conductor(s) must be sufficient.
[p102.b15] Unless local wiring regulations state otherwise, the cross-sectional area of the protective earth conductor must agree with the conditions that require automatic disconnection of the supply required in 411.3.2 of IEC 60364-4-41:2005 and be capable of withstanding the prospective fault current during the disconnection time of the protective device. The cross-sectional area of the protective earth conductor must be selected from the table below or calculated according to 543.1 of IEC 60364-5-54.
[p102.b16] This table shows the minimum cross-sectional area of the protective earth conductor related to the phase conductor size according to IEC/UL 61800-5-1 when the phase conductor(s) and the protective earth conductor are made of the same metal. If this is not so, the cross-sectional area of the protective earth conductor must be determined

[p103.b10] ￭Additional grounding requirements – IEC
[p103.b11] This section gives grounding requirements according to standard IEC/EN 61800-5-1.
[p103.b12] Because the normal touch current of the drive is more than 3.5 mA AC or 10 mA DC:
[p103.b13] • the minimum size of the protective earth conductor must comply with the local safety regulations for high protective earth conductor current equipment, and
[p103.b14] • you must use one of these connection methods:
[p103.b15] (step 1) 1. a fixed connection and:
[p103.b16] • a protective earth conductor with a minimum cross-sectional area of 10 mm2
[p103.b17] Cu or 16 mm2 Al (as an alternative when aluminum cables are permitted), or
[p103.b18] • a second protective earth conductor of the same cross-sectional area as the original protective earth conductor, or
[p103.b19] • a device that automatically disconnects the supply if the protective earth conductor is damaged.
[p103.b20] (step 2) 2. a connection with an industrial connector according to IEC 60309 and a minimum protective earth conductor cross-section of 2.5 mm2 as part of a multi-conductor power cable. Sufficient strain relief must be provided.

[p104.b5] This section gives grounding requirements according to standard UL 61800-5-1.
[p104.b6] The protective earth conductor must be sized as specified in Article 250.122 and table 250.122 of the National Electric Code, ANSI/NFPA 70.
[p104.b7] For cord-connected equipment, it must not be possible to disconnect the protective earth conductor before power is removed.
[p104.b8] Selecting the control cables
[p104.b9] ￭Shielding
[p104.b10] Only use shielded control cables.
[p104.b11] Use a double-shielded twisted pair cable for analog signals. ABB recommends this type of cable also for the pulse encoder signals. Use one individually shielded pair for each signal. Do not use common return for different analog signals.
[p104.b12] A double-shielded cable (a) is the best alternative for low-voltage digital signals, but single-shielded (b) twisted pair cable is also acceptable.
[p104.b13] a b
[p104.b14] ￭Signals in separate cables
[p104.b15] Run analog and digital signals in separate, shielded cables. Do not mix 24 V DC and 115/230 V AC signals in the same cable.
[p104.b16] ￭Signals that can be run in the same cable
[p104.b17] If their voltage does not exceed 48 V, relay-controlled signals can be run in the same cables as digital input signals. The relay-controlled signals should be run as twisted pairs.

[p105.b1] Guidelines for planning the electrical installation 101
[p105.b2] ￭Relay cable
[p105.b3] The cable type with braided metallic shield (for example ÖLFLEX by LAPPKABEL, Germany) has been tested and approved by ABB.
[p105.b4] ￭Control panel to drive cable
[p105.b5] Use EIA-485, Cat 5e (or better) cable with male RJ-45 connectors. The maximum length of the cable is 100 m (328 ft).
[p105.b6] ￭PC tool cable
[p105.b7] Connect the Drive Composer PC tool to the drive through the USB port of the control panel. Use a USB Type A (PC) - Type Mini-B (control panel) cable. The maximum length of the cable is 3 m (9.8 ft).
[p105.b8] ￭FPBA-01 PROFIBUS DP adapter module connectors
[p105.b9] Frames R1…R3: The following connector types have been tested to fit in the tight space for option slot 1.
[p105.b10] • Phoenix Contact SUBCON-PLUS-PROFIB/PG/SC2, part number 2708245. Lead the cable through the control cable hole on the right in the entry plate (1).
[p105.b11] • Siemens, part number 6GK1 500 0EA02. Lead the cable through the middle control cable hole in the entry plate (2).

[p105.b13] Routing the cables
[p105.b14] ￭General guidelines – IEC
[p105.b15] • Route the motor cable away from other cables. Motor cables of several drives can be run in parallel installed next to each other.
[p105.b16] • Install the motor cable, input power cable and control cables on separate trays.
[p105.b17] • Avoid long parallel runs of motor cables with other cables.
=== page 106 ===
[p106.b1] 102 Guidelines for planning the electrical installation
[p106.b2] • Where control cables must cross power cables, make sure that they are arranged at an angle as near to 90 degrees as possible.
[p106.b3] • Do not run extra cables through the drive.
[p106.b4] • Make sure that the cable trays have good electrical bonding to each other and to the grounding electrodes. Aluminum tray systems can be used to improve local equalizing of potential.

[p107.b5] ￭Continuous motor cable shield/conduit or enclosure for equipment on the motor cable
[p107.b6] To minimize the emission level when safety switches, contactors, connection boxes or similar equipment are installed on the motor cable between the drive and the motor:
[p107.b7] • Install the equipment in a metal enclosure.
[p107.b8] • Use either a symmetrical shielded cable, or install the cabling in a metal conduit.
[p107.b9] • Make sure that there is a good and continuous galvanic connection in the shield/conduit between drive and motor.
[p107.b10] • Connect the shield/conduit to the protective ground terminal of the drive and the motor.

[p108.b2] ￭Separate control cable ducts
[p108.b3] Put 24 V DC and 230 V AC (120 V AC) control cables in separate ducts, unless the 24 V DC cable is insulated for 230 V AC (120 V AC) or insulated with an insulation sleeving for 230 V AC (120 V AC).

[p108.b7] Implementing short-circuit and thermal overload protection
[p108.b8] ￭Protecting the drive and the input power cable in short-circuits
[p108.b9] Protect the drive with fuses and the input cable with fuses or a circuit breaker.
[p108.b10] ~ ~ M 3~
[p108.b11] Size the fuses or circuit breakers according to local regulations for the input cable protection. Select the fuses or circuit breakers for the drive according to the instructions given in the technical data. The fuses for the drive protection will restrict drive damage and prevent damage to adjoining equipment in case of a short-circuit inside the drive.
[p108.b12] Note: If the fuses or circuit breakers for the drive protection are placed at the distribution board and the input cable is dimensioned according to the nominal input current of the drive given in the technical data, the fuses or circuit breakers protect also the input cable in short-circuit situations, restrict drive damage and prevent damage to adjoining equipment in case of a short-circuit inside the drive. No separate fuses or circuit breakers for the input cable protection are needed.
[p108.b13] WARNING! Due to the inherent operating principle and construction of circuit breakers, independent of the manufacturer, hot ionized gases can escape from the breaker enclosure in case of a short-circuit. To ensure safe use, pay special attention to the installation and placement of the breakers. Obey the manufacturer’s instructions.
=== page 109 ===
[p109.b1] Guidelines for planning the electrical installation 105
[p109.b2] ￭Protecting the motor and motor cable in short-circuits
[p109.b3] The drive protects the motor cable and motor in a short-circuit situation when the motor cable is sized according to the nominal output current of the drive.
[p109.b4] ￭Protecting the motor cables against thermal overload
[p109.b5] The drive protects the motor cables against thermal overload when the cables are sized according to the nominal output current of the drive. No additional thermal protection devices are needed.
[p109.b6] WARNING! If the drive is connected to multiple motors, use a separate overload protection for each motor cable and motor. The drive overload protection is tuned for the total motor load. It may not detect an overload in one motor circuit only.
[p109.b7] North America: The local code (NEC) requires an overload protection and a short-circuit protection for each motor circuit. Use, for example:
[p109.b8] • a manual motor protector
[p109.b9] • circuit breaker, contactor and overload relay or
[p109.b10] • fuses, contactor and overload relay.
[p109.b11] ￭Protecting the motor against thermal overload
[p109.b12] According to regulations, the motor must be protected against thermal overload and the current must be switched off when overload is detected. The drive includes a motor thermal protection function that protects the motor and switches off the current when necessary. Depending on a drive parameter value, the function either monitors a calculated temperature value (based on a motor thermal model) or an actual temperature indication given by motor temperature sensors.
[p109.b13] The motor thermal protection model supports thermal memory retention and speed sensitivity. The user can tune the thermal model further by feeding in additional motor and load data.
[p109.b14] The most common temperature sensor types are PTC or Pt100.
[p109.b15] For more information, see the firmware manual.
[p109.b16] ￭Protecting the motor against overload without thermal model or temperature sensors
[p109.b17] Motor overload protection protects the motor against overload without using motor thermal model or temperature sensors.
[p109.b18] Motor overload protection is required and specified by multiple standards including the US National Electric Code (NEC) and the common UL/IEC 61800-5-1 standard in
=== page 110 ===
[p110.b1] 106 Guidelines for planning the electrical installation [p110.b2] conjunction with UL/IEC 60947-4-1. The standards allow for motor overload protection without external temperature sensors.
[p110.b3] The protection feature allows the user to specify the class of operation in the same manner as the overload relays are specified in standards UL/IEC 60947-4-1 and NEMA ICS 2.
[p110.b4] The motor overload protection supports thermal memory retention and speed sensitivity.
[p110.b5] For more information, see drive firmware manual.
[p110.b6] Protecting the drive against ground faults
[p110.b7] The drive is equipped with an internal ground fault protective function to protect the unit against ground faults in the motor and motor cable. This function is not a personnel safety or a fire protection feature. See the firmware manual for more information.
[p110.b8] ￭Residual current device compatibility
[p110.b9] The drive is suitable to be used with residual current devices of Type B.
[p110.b10] Note: As standard, the drive contains capacitors connected between the main circuit and the frame. These capacitors and long motor cables increase the ground leakage current and may cause nuisance faults in residual current devices.
[p110.b11] Implementing the emergency stop function
[p110.b12] For safety reasons, install the emergency stop devices at each operator control station and at other operating stations where the emergency stop may be needed. Implement the emergency stop according to relevant standards.
[p110.b13] Note: You can use the Safe torque off function of the drive to implement the Emergency stop function.
[p110.b14] Implementing the Safe torque off function
[p110.b15] See The Safe torque off function (page 347).
[p110.b16] Implementing an ATEX-certified motor thermal protection
[p110.b17] With option +Q971, the drive provides ATEX-certified safe motor disconnection without contactor using the drive Safe torque off function. To implement the thermal protection of a motor in explosive atmosphere (Ex motor), you must also:
[p110.b18] • use an ATEX-certified Ex motor
[p110.b19] • order an ATEX-certified thermistor protection module for the drive (option +L537), or acquire and install an ATEX-compliant protection relay
[p110.b20] • do the necessary connections.
[p110.b21] For more information, see:

[p111.b4] Using a safety switch between the drive and the motor
[p111.b5] ABB recommends to install a safety switch between the permanent magnet motor and the drive output. The switch is needed to isolate the motor from the drive during maintenance work on the drive.
[p111.b6] Implementing the Power-loss ride-through function
[p111.b7] See the firmware manual.
[p111.b8] Controlling a contactor between drive and motor
[p111.b9] The control of the output contactor depends on how you use the drive, that is, which motor control mode and which motor stop mode you select.
[p111.b10] If you have the vector control mode and motor ramp stop selected, open the contactor as follows:
[p111.b11] (step 1) 1. Give a stop command to the drive.
[p111.b12] (step 2) 2. Wait until the drive decelerates the motor to zero speed.
[p111.b13] (step 3) 3. Open the contactor.
[p111.b14] If you have the vector control mode and motor coast stop, or scalar control mode selected, open the contactor as follows:
[p111.b15] (step 1) 1. Give a stop command to the drive.
[p111.b16] (step 2) 2. Open the contactor.
[p111.b17] WARNING! When the vector control mode is in use, never open the output contactor while the drive controls the motor. The vector control operates extremely fast, much faster than it takes for the contactor to open its contacts. When the contactor starts opening while the drive controls the motor, the vector control will try to maintain the load current by immediately increasing the drive output voltage to the maximum. This will damage, or even burn, the contactor completely.
[p111.b18] Implementing a bypass connection
[p111.b19] If bypassing is required, employ mechanically or electrically interlocked contactors between the motor and the drive and between the motor and the power line. Make sure
=== page 112 ===
[p112.b1] 108 Guidelines for planning the electrical installation [p112.b2] with interlocking that the contactors cannot be closed simultaneously. The installation must be clearly marked as defined in IEC/EN/UL 61800-5-1, subclause 6.5.3, for example, “THIS MACHINE STARTS AUTOMATICALLY”.
[p112.b3] WARNING! Never connect the drive output to the electrical power network. The connection may damage the drive.

[p113.b4] Switching the motor power supply from drive to direct-on-line
[p113.b5] (step 1) 1. Stop the drive and the motor with the drive control panel stop key (drive in the local control mode) or the external stop signal (drive in the remote control mode).
[p113.b6] (step 2) 2. Open the main contactor of the drive with S11.
[p113.b7] (step 3) 3. Switch the motor power supply from the drive to direct-on-line with S40.
[p113.b8] (step 4) 4. Wait for 10 seconds to allow the motor magnetization to dissipate.
[p113.b9] (step 5) 5. Start the motor with S41.
[p113.b10] Switching the motor power supply from direct-on-line to drive
[p113.b11] (step 1) 1. Stop the motor with S42.
[p113.b12] (step 2) 2. Switch the motor power supply from direct-on-line to the drive with S40.
[p113.b13] (step 3) 3. Close the main contactor of the drive with switch S11 (-> turn to position ST for two seconds and leave to position 1).
[p113.b14] (step 4) 4. Start the drive and the motor with the drive control panel start key (drive in the local control mode) or the external start signal (drive in the remote control mode).
[p113.b15] Protecting the contacts of relay outputs
[p113.b16] Inductive loads (relays, contactors, motors) cause voltage transients when switched off.
[p113.b17] Install the protective component as close to the inductive load as possible. Do not install protective components at the relay outputs.

[p114.b8] Implementing a motor temperature sensor connection
[p114.b9] WARNING! IEC 61800-5-1 requires double or reinforced insulation between live parts and accessible parts when:
[p114.b10] • the accessible parts are not conductive, or
[p114.b11] • the accessible parts are conductive, but not connected to the protective earth.
[p114.b12] Obey this requirement when you plan the connection of the motor temperature sensor to the drive.
[p114.b13] To connect a motor temperature sensor and other similar components to the drive, you have four alternatives:
[p114.b14] (step 1) 1. If there is double or reinforced insulation between the sensor and the live parts of the motor, you can connect the sensor directly to the inputs of the drive.
[p114.b15] (step 2) 2. If there is basic insulation between the sensor and the live parts of the motor, you can connect the sensor to the analog/digital inputs of the drive if all circuits connected to the drive’s digital and analog inputs (typically extra-low voltage circuits) are
=== page 115 ===
[p115.b1] Guidelines for planning the electrical installation 111 [p115.b2] protected against contact and insulated with basic insulation from other low-voltage circuits. The insulation must be rated for the same voltage level as the drive main circuit. Note that extra-low voltage circuits (such as 24 V DC) typically do not meet these requirements.
[p115.b3] (step 3) 3. You can connect the sensor to the drive via an option module.The sensor and the module must form a double or reinforced insulation between the motor live parts and the drive control unit. See section Connection of motor temperature sensor to the drive via an option module (page 100).
[p115.b4] (step 4) 4. You can connect the sensor to a digital input of the drive via a customer’s external relay. The sensor and the relay must form a double or reinforced insulation between the motor live parts and the drive control unit. See section Connection of motor temperature sensor to the drive via a relay (page 101).

[p117.b3] Electrical installation – IEC
[p117.b4] Contents of this chapter
[p117.b5] This chapter describes how to:
[p117.b6] • measure the insulation
[p117.b7] • do the grounding system compatibility check
[p117.b8] • change the EMC filter or ground-to-phase varistor connection
[p117.b9] • connect the power and control cables
[p117.b10] • install optional modules
[p117.b11] • connect a PC.
[p117.b12] Warnings
[p117.b13] WARNING! Obey the safety instructions of the drive. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur. If you are not a qualified electrical professional, do not do installation, commissioning or maintenance work.
[p117.b14] Required tools
[p117.b15] To do the electrical installation, you need these tools:
[p117.b16] • wire stripper
[p117.b17] • screwdriver set (Torx, flat and/or Phillips, as appropriate)
[p117.b18] • torque wrench.
=== page 118 ===
[p118.b1] 114 Electrical installation – IEC
[p118.b2] Grounding the motor cable shield at the motor end
[p118.b3] For minimum radio-frequency interference, ground the cable shield 360 degrees at the cable entry of the motor terminal box.
[p118.b4] Measuring the insulation
[p118.b5] ￭Measuring the insulation resistance of the drive
[p118.b6] WARNING! Do not do any voltage withstand or insulation resistance tests on any part of the drive as testing can damage the drive. Every drive has been tested for insulation between the main circuit and the chassis at the factory. Also, there are voltage-limiting circuits inside the drive which cut down the testing voltage automatically.
[p118.b7] ￭Measuring the insulation resistance of the input power cable
[p118.b8] Before you connect the input power cable to the drive, measure its insulation resistance according to local regulations.
[p118.b9] ￭Measuring the insulation resistance of the motor and motor cable
[p118.b10] WARNING! Obey the safety instructions of the drive. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur. If you are not a qualified electrical professional, do not do installation, commissioning or maintenance work.
[p118.b11] (step 1) 1. Do the steps in section Electrical safety precautions (page 22) before you start the work.
[p118.b12] (step 2) 2. Make sure that the motor cable is disconnected from the drive output terminals.
[p118.b13] (step 3) 3. Measure the insulation resistance between each phase conductor and the protective earth conductor. Use a measuring voltage of 1000 V DC. The insulation resistance of an ABB motor must be more than 100 Mohm (reference value at 25 °C [77 °F]). For the insulation resistance of other motors, refer to the manufacturer’s instructions.
[p118.b14] Note: Moisture inside the motor reduces the insulation resistance. If you think that there is moisture in the motor, dry the motor and do the measurement again.

[p119.b19] Grounding system compatibility check
[p119.b20] The standard drive can be an be installed to a symmetrically grounded TN-S system. For other systems, see sections EMC filter and Ground-to-phase varistors (page 116) below.
[p119.b21] ￭EMC filter
[p119.b22] A drive with EMC filter connected can be installed to a symmetrically grounded TN-S system. If you install the drive to another system, you may need to disconnect the EMC
=== page 120 ===
[p120.b1] 116 Electrical installation – IEC [p120.b2] filter. See sections When to disconnect EMC filter or ground-to-phase varistor: TN-S, IT, corner-grounded delta and midpoint-grounded delta systems (page 116), and Guidelines for installing the drive to a TT system (page 117).
[p120.b3] WARNING! Do not install the drive with the EMC filter connected to a system that the filter is not suitable for. This can cause danger, or damage the drive.
[p120.b4] Note: When the internal EMC filter is disconnected, the drive EMC compatibility is considerably reduced. See EMC compatibility and motor cable length (page 290).
[p120.b5] ￭Ground-to-phase varistors
[p120.b6] A drive with the ground-to-phase varistor connected can be installed to a symmetrically grounded TN-S system. If you install the drive to another system, you may need to disconnect the varistor. [p120.b7] WARNING! Do not install the drive with the ground-to-phase varistor connected to a system that the varistor is not suitable for. If you do, the varistor circuit can be damaged.

[p121.b10] ￭Guidelines for installing the drive to a TT system
[p121.b11] The drive can be installed to a TT system under these conditions:
[p121.b12] (step 1) 1. Residual current device has been installed in the supply system.
[p121.b13] (step 2) 2. These screws have been disconnected. Otherwise EMC filter and ground-to-phase varistor capacitor leakage current will cause the residual current device to trip.

[p123.b1] Electrical installation – IEC 119
[p123.b2] ￭Identifying the grounding system of the electrical power network
[p123.b3] WARNING! Only a qualified electrical professional may do the work instructed in this section. Depending on the installation site, the work may even be categorized as live working. Continue only if you are an electrical professional certified for the work. Obey the local regulations. If you ignore them, injury or death can occur.
[p123.b4] To identify the grounding system, examine the supply transformer connection. See the applicable electrical diagrams of the building. If that is not possible, measure these voltages at the distribution board, and use the table to define the grounding system type.
[p123.b5] (step 1) 1. input voltage line to line (UL-L)
[p123.b6] (step 2) 2. input voltage line 1 to ground (UL1-G)
[p123.b7] (step 3) 3. input voltage line 2 to ground (UL2-G)
[p123.b8] (step 4) 4. input voltage line 3 to ground (UL3-G).
[p123.b9] The table below shows the line-to-ground voltages in relation to the line-to-line voltage for each grounding system.

[p123.b17] ￭Disconnecting internal EMC filter or ground-to-phase varistor - frames R1…R3
[p123.b18] To disconnect the internal EMC filter or ground-to-phase varistor, if needed, do as follows:

[p123.b21] (step 3) 3. To disconnect the internal EMC filter, remove the EMC screw (3a) and place it in the storage place (3b).

=== page 141 ===
[p141.b1] Electrical installation – IEC 137
[p141.b2] Terminals T1/U, T2/V and T3/W
[p141.b3] • Remove the nut that attaches the connector to its busbar.
[p141.b4] • Put the conductor under the connector pressure plate and pre-tighten the conductor.
[p141.b5] • Put the connector back to its busbar. Start the nut, and turn it at least two rotations by hand.
[p141.b6] WARNING! Before using tools, make sure that the nut/screw is not cross-threading. Cross-threading will damage the drive and cause danger.
[p141.b7] • Tighten the nut to a torque of 30 N·m (22 lbf·ft).
[p141.b8] • Tighten the conductor(s) to 40 N·m (30 lbf·ft) for frame R8 or to 70 N·m (52 lbf·ft) for frame R9.
[p141.b9] Terminals L1, L2 and L3
[p141.b10] • Remove the combi screw that attaches the connector to its terminal post, and pull the connector off.
[p141.b11] • Put the conductor under the connector pressure plate and pre-tighten the conductor.
[p141.b12] • Put the connector back onto the terminal post. Start the combi screw, and turn it at least two rotations by hand.
[p141.b13] WARNING! Before using tools, make sure that the nut/screw is not cross-threading. Cross-threading will damage the drive and cause danger.
[p141.b14] • Tighten the combi screw to a torque of 30 N·m (22 lbf·ft).
[p141.b15] • Tighten the conductor(s) to 40 N·m (30 lbf·ft) for frame R8 or to 70 N·m (52 lbf·ft) for frame R9.
[p141.b16] (step 11) 11. Frames R8…R9: If you install parallel cables, install the second grounding shelf for the parallel power cables (11a). Repeat steps 6…11 (11b).

[p152.b6] ￭Control cable connection procedure R1…R9
[p152.b7] WARNING! Obey the safety instructions of the drive. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur.
[p152.b8] (step 1) 1. Do the steps in section Electrical safety precautions (page 22) before you start the work.
[p152.b9] (step 2) 2. Remove the front cover(s) if not already removed. See page 123 (R1…R4), page 129 (R5) or page 81 (R6…R9). Analog signals The figures for frames R1…R2 and R3 (page 150), R4 (page 151), R5 (page 152) and R6…R9 (page 153) show an example of connecting a cable. Make the connections according to the macro in use.
[p152.b10] (step 3) 3. Cut an adequate hole into the rubber grommet and slide the grommet onto the cable. Slide the cable through a hole in the cable entry and attach the grommet to the hole.
[p152.b11] (step 4) 4. Ground the outer shield of the cable 360 degrees under the grounding clamp. Keep the cable unstripped as close to the terminals of the control unit as possible. Frames R5…R9: Secure the cables mechanically at the clamps below the control unit. Ground also the pair-cable shields and grounding wire at the SCR terminal.
[p152.b12] (step 5) 5. Route the cable as shown in the figures for frames R1…R2 and R3 (page 150), R4 (page 151), R5 (page 152) and R6…R9 (page 153).
[p152.b13] (step 6) 6. Connect the conductors to the appropriate terminals of the control unit and tighten to 0.5…0.6 N·m (0.4 lbf·ft). Digital signals The figures for frames R1…R2 and R3 (page 150), R4 (page 151), R5 (page 152) and R6…R9 (page 153) show an example of connecting a cable. [p153.b1] Electrical installation – IEC 149
[p153.b2] (step 7) 7. Cut an adequate hole into the rubber grommet and slide the grommet onto the cable. Slide the cable through the hole in the cable entry and attach the grommet to the hole.
[p153.b3] (step 8) 8. Ground the outer shield of the cable 360 degrees under the grounding clamp. Keep the cable unstripped as close to the terminals of the control unit as possible. Frames R5…R9: Secure the cables mechanically at the clamps below the control unit. If you use double-shielded cables, ground also the pair-cable shields and grounding wire at the SCR terminal.
[p153.b4] (step 9) 9. Route the cable as shown in the figures for frames R1…R2 and R3 (page 150), R4 (page 151), R5 (page 152) and R6…R9 (page 153).
[p153.b5] (step 10) 10. Connect the conductors to the appropriate terminals of the control unit and tighten to 0.5…0.6 N·m (0.4 lbf·ft).
[p153.b6] (step 11) 11. Tie all control cables to the provided cable tie mounts.
[p153.b7] Note:
[p153.b8] • Leave the other ends of the control cable shields unconnected or ground them indirectly via a high-frequency capacitor with a few nanofarads, eg, 3.3 nF / 630 V. The shield can also be grounded directly at both ends if they are in the same ground line with no significant voltage drop between the end points.
[p153.b9] • Keep any signal wire pairs twisted as close to the terminals as possible. Twisting the wire with its return wire reduces disturbances caused by inductive coupling.

[p165.b1] Electrical installation – IEC 161
[p165.b2] A PC (with eg, the Drive composer PC tool) can be connected as follows:
[p165.b3] (step 1) 1. Connect a ACS-AP-… or ACH-AP-… control panel to the unit either
[p165.b4] • by inserting the control panel into the panel holder or platform, or
[p165.b5] • by using an Ethernet (eg, Cat 5e) networking cable.
[p165.b6] (step 2) 2. Remove the USB connector cover on the front of the control panel.
[p165.b7] (step 3) 3. Connect an USB cable (Type A to Type Mini-B) between the USB connector on the control panel (3a) and a free USB port on the PC (3b).
[p165.b8] (step 4) 4. The panel will display an indication whenever the connection is active.
[p165.b9] (step 5) 5. See the documentation of the PC tool for setup instructions.

[p167.b3] Electrical installation – North America
[p167.b4] Contents of this chapter
[p167.b5] This chapter describes how to:
[p167.b6] • measure the insulation
[p167.b7] • do the grounding system compatibility check
[p167.b8] • change the EMC filter or ground-to-phase varistor connection
[p167.b9] • connect the power and control cables
[p167.b10] • install optional modules
[p167.b11] • connect a PC.
[p167.b12] Warnings
[p167.b13] WARNING! Obey the safety instructions of the drive. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur. If you are not a qualified electrical professional, do not do installation, commissioning or maintenance work.
=== page 168 ===
[p168.b1] 164 Electrical installation – North America
[p168.b2] Required tools
[p168.b3] To do the electrical installation, you need these tools:
[p168.b4] • wire stripper
[p168.b5] • screwdriver set (Torx, flat and/or Phillips, as appropriate)
[p168.b6] • torque wrench.
[p168.b7] Grounding the motor cable shield at the motor end
[p168.b8] For minimum radio-frequency interference, ground the cable shield 360 degrees at the cable entry of the motor terminal box.
[p168.b9] Measuring the insulation
[p168.b10] Measuring the insulation is typically not required in North American installations.
[p168.b11] ￭Measuring the insulation resistance of the drive
[p168.b12] WARNING! Do not do any voltage withstand or insulation resistance tests on any part of the drive as testing can damage the drive. Every drive has been tested for insulation between the main circuit and the chassis at the factory. Also, there are voltage-limiting circuits inside the drive which cut down the testing voltage automatically.
[p168.b13] ￭Measuring the insulation resistance of the input power cable
[p168.b14] Before you connect the input power cable to the drive, measure its insulation resistance according to local regulations.
[p168.b15] ￭Measuring the insulation resistance of the motor and motor cable
[p168.b16] WARNING! Obey the safety instructions of the drive. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur. If you are not a qualified electrical professional, do not do installation, commissioning or maintenance work.
=== page 169 ===
[p169.b1] Electrical installation – North America 165
[p169.b2] (step 1) 1. Do the steps in section Electrical safety precautions (page 22) before you start the work.
[p169.b3] (step 2) 2. Make sure that the motor cable is disconnected from the drive output terminals.
[p169.b4] (step 3) 3. Measure the insulation resistance between each phase conductor and the protective earth conductor. Use a measuring voltage of 1000 V DC. The insulation resistance of an ABB motor must be more than 100 Mohm (reference value at 25 °C [77 °F]). For the insulation resistance of other motors, refer to the manufacturer’s instructions.
[p169.b5] Note: Moisture inside the motor reduces the insulation resistance. If you think that there is moisture in the motor, dry the motor and do the measurement again.

[p169.b13] ￭Brake resistor assembly for R1…R3
[p169.b14] WARNING! Obey the safety instructions of the drive. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur. If you are not a qualified electrical professional, do not do installation, commissioning or maintenance work.
[p169.b15] (step 1) 1. Stop the drive and do the steps in section Electrical safety precautions (page 22) before you start the work.
[p169.b16] (step 2) 2. Make sure that the resistor cable is connected to the resistor and disconnected from the drive output terminals.
[p169.b17] (step 3) 3. At the drive end, connect the R+ and R- conductors of the resistor cable together. Measure the insulation resistance between the conductors and the PE conductor with a measuring voltage of 1000 V DC. The insulation resistance must be more than 1 Mohm.

=== page 170 ===
[p170.b1] 166 Electrical installation – North America
[p170.b2] Grounding system compatibility check
[p170.b3] The standard drive can be an be installed to a symmetrically grounded TN-S system.
[p170.b4] For other systems, see sections EMC filter and Ground-to-phase varistors below.
[p170.b5] ￭EMC filter
[p170.b6] To connect the drive to symmetrically grounded TN-S systems, you should connect the internal EMC filter if you are concerned with EMC issues. See section When to connect EMC filter or disconnect ground-to-phase varistor: TN-S, IT, corner-grounded delta and midpoint-grounded delta systems (page 166).
[p170.b7] WARNING! Do not install the drive with the EMC filter connected to a system that the filter is not suitable for. This can cause danger, or damage the drive.
[p170.b8] Note: When the internal EMC filter is disconnected, the drive EMC compatibility is considerably reduced.
[p170.b9] ￭Ground-to-phase varistors
[p170.b10] A drive with the ground-to-phase varistor connected can be installed to a symmetrically grounded TN-S system. If you install the drive to another system, you may need to disconnect the varistor. See When to connect EMC filter or disconnect ground-to-phase varistor: TN-S, IT, corner-grounded delta and midpoint-grounded delta systems (page 166), and Guidelines for installing the drive to a TT system (page 168).
[p170.b11] WARNING! Do not install the drive with the ground-to-phase varistor connected to a system that the varistor is not suitable for. If you do, the varistor circuit can be damaged.
[p170.b12] ￭When to connect EMC filter or disconnect ground-to-phase varistor: TN-S, IT, corner-grounded delta and midpoint-grounded delta systems
[p170.b13] Requirements for disconnecting EMC filter and varistor and additional requirements for different electrical power systems are given below.
[p170.b14] Note: Configure the EMC filter based on the electrical system of the installation site.

[p171.b11] Note: The VAR screw on R1…R3 also connects the EMC (AC) circuit internally within the drive.
[p171.b12] Note: Failure to remove a metal screw, when indicated in the table above, may result in drive failure.

[p172.b6] ￭Guidelines for installing the drive to a TT system
[p172.b7] The drive can be installed to a TT system under these conditions:
[p172.b8] (step 1) 1. Residual current device has been installed in the supply system.
[p172.b9] (step 2) 2. EMC filter screws have been disconnected (= they are plastic screws or there is no screw). Otherwise EMC filter leakage current will cause the residual current device to trip. For R1…R3, the VAR screw must be plastic, and for R4…R9, the VAR screw must be metal.

[p172.b14] • ABB does not guarantee the EMC category because the EMC filter screws have been disconnected.
[p172.b15] • ABB does not guarantee the functioning of the ground leakage detector built inside the drive.
[p172.b16] • In large systems the residual current device can trip without a real reason.

[p173.b2] ￭Identifying the grounding system of the electrical power network
[p173.b3] WARNING! Only a qualified electrical professional may do the work instructed in this section. Depending on the installation site, the work may even be categorized as live working. Continue only if you are an electrical professional certified for the work. Obey the local regulations. If you ignore them, injury or death can occur.
[p173.b4] To identify the grounding system, examine the supply transformer connection. See the applicable electrical diagrams of the building. If that is not possible, measure these voltages at the distribution board, and use the table to define the grounding system type.
[p173.b5] (step 1) 1. input voltage line to line (UL-L)
[p173.b6] (step 2) 2. input voltage line 1 to ground (UL1-G)
[p173.b7] (step 3) 3. input voltage line 2 to ground (UL2-G)
[p173.b8] (step 4) 4. input voltage line 3 to ground (UL3-G).
[p173.b9] The table below shows the line-to-ground voltages in relation to the line-to-line voltage for each grounding system.

[p189.b9] Detaching and reinstalling the connectors
[p189.b10] This is possible but not recommended. Terminals T1/U, T2/V and T3/W
[p189.b11] • Remove the nut that attaches the connector to its busbar.
[p189.b12] • Put the conductor under the connector pressure plate and pre-tighten the conductor.
[p189.b13] • Put the connector back to its busbar. Start the nut, and turn it at least two rotations by hand.
[p189.b14] WARNING! Before using tools, make sure that the nut/screw is not cross-threading. Cross-threading will damage the drive and cause danger.
[p189.b15] • Tighten the nut to a torque of 30 N·m (22 lbf·ft).
[p189.b16] • Tighten the conductor(s) to 40 N·m (30 lbf·ft) for frame R8 or to 70 N·m (52 lbf·ft) for frame R9.
[p189.b17] Terminals L1, L2 and L3
[p189.b18] • Remove the combi screw that attaches the connector to its terminal post, and pull the connector off.
[p189.b19] • Put the conductor under the connector pressure plate and pre-tighten the conductor.
[p189.b20] • Put the connector back onto the terminal post. Start the combi screw, and turn it at least two rotations by hand.
[p189.b21] WARNING! Before using tools, make sure that the nut/screw is not cross-threading. Cross-threading will damage the drive and cause danger.
=== page 190 ===
[p190.b1] 186 Electrical installation – North America
[p190.b2] • Tighten the combi screw to a torque of 30 N·m (22 lbf·ft).
[p190.b3] • Tighten the conductor(s) to 40 N·m (30 lbf·ft) for frame R8 or to 70 N·m (52 lbf·ft) for frame R9.

[p196.b8] Connection for obtaining 0…10 V from analog output 2 (AO2)
[p196.b9] To obtain 0…10 V from analog output AO2, connect a 500 ohm resistor (or two 1 kohm resistors in parallel) between the analog output 2 AO2 and analog common ground AGND.

The macro wiring diagrams on these pages use an externally powered sensor (connections not shown). The figures below give examples of connections using a two-wire or three-wire sensor/transmitter supplied by the drive auxiliary voltage output.

=== page 199 ===
[p199.b1] Electrical installation – North America 195
[p199.b2] WARNING! As the inputs pictured above are not insulated according to IEC 60664, the connection of the motor temperature sensor requires double or reinforced insulation between motor live parts and the sensor. If the assembly does not fulfill the requirement, the I/O board terminals must be protected against contact and must not be connected to other equipment or the temperature sensor must be isolated from the I/O terminals.
[p199.b3] Safe torque off (X4)
[p199.b4] For the drive to start, both connections (+24 V DC to IN1 and +24 V DC to IN2) must be closed. By default, the terminal block has jumpers to close the circuit. Remove the jumpers before connecting an external Safe torque off circuitry to the drive. See chapter The Safe torque off function (page 347).
[p199.b5] Note: Only 24 V DC can be used for STO. Only PNP input configuration can be used.
[p199.b6] ￭Control cable connection procedure R1…R9
[p199.b7] WARNING! Obey the safety instructions of the drive. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur.
[p199.b8] (step 1) 1. Do the steps in section Electrical safety precautions (page 22) before you start the work.
[p199.b9] (step 2) 2. Remove the front cover(s) if not already removed. See page 174 (R1…R4), page 178 (R5) or page 81 (R6…R9). Analog signals The figures for frames R1…R2 and R3 (page 197), R4 (page 198), R5 (page 199) and R6…R9 (page 200) show an example of connecting a cable. Make the connections according to the macro in use.
[p199.b10] (step 3) 3. Remove the rubber grommets from the cable entry for the cables to be connected. Attach cable conduits to the empty cable entry holes. Slide the cables through the cable conduits.
[p199.b11] (step 4) 4. Frames R5…R9: Secure the cables mechanically at the clamps below the control unit. Ground also the pair-cable shields and grounding wire at the SCR terminal, or either, you may ground the shield at the source of the signal, but do not ground it at both the source of the signal and the SCR terminal.
[p199.b12] (step 5) 5. Route the cable as shown in the figures for frames R1…R2 and R3 (page 197), R4 (page 198), R5 (page 199) and R6…R9 (page 200).
[p199.b13] (step 6) 6. Connect the conductors to the appropriate terminals of the control unit and tighten to 0.5…0.6 N·m (0.4 lbf·ft).
=== page 200 ===
[p200.b1] 196 Electrical installation – North America
[p200.b2] Digital signals The figures for frames R1…R2 and R3 (page 197), R4 (page 198), R5 (page 199) and R6…R9 (page 200) show an example of connecting a cable. Make the connections according to the macro in use.
[p200.b3] (step 7) 7. Remove the rubber grommets from the cable entry for the cables to be connected. Attach cable conduits to the empty cable entry holes. Slide the cables through the cable conduits.
[p200.b4] (step 8) 8. Frames R5…R9: Secure the cables mechanically at the clamps below the control unit. If you use double-shielded cables, ground also the pair-cable shields and grounding wire at the SCR terminal.
[p200.b5] (step 9) 9. Route the cable as shown in the figures for frames R1…R2 and R3 (page 197), R4 (page 198), R5 (page 199) and R6…R9 (page 200).
[p200.b6] (step 10) 10. Connect the conductors to the appropriate terminals of the control unit and tighten to 0.5…0.6 N·m (0.4 lbf·ft).
[p200.b7] (step 11) 11. Tie all control cables to the provided cable tie mounts.
[p200.b8] Note:
[p200.b9] • Leave the other ends of the control cable shields unconnected or ground them indirectly via a high-frequency capacitor with a few nanofarads, eg, 3.3 nF / 630 V. The shield can also be grounded directly at both ends if they are in the same ground line with no significant voltage drop between the end points.
[p200.b10] • Keep any signal wire pairs twisted as close to the terminals as possible. Twisting the wire with its return wire reduces disturbances caused by inductive coupling.

[p205.b2] Installing option modules
[p205.b3] Note: In North American deliveries, options may also be ordered as factory installed.
[p205.b4] Note: If you will install the FPBA-01 module, see section FPBA-01 PROFIBUS DP adapter module connectors (page 101) for suitable connector types.
[p205.b5] ￭Mechanical installation of option modules
[p205.b6] See section Overview of power and control connections (page 42) for the available slots for each module. Install the option modules as follows:
[p205.b7] WARNING! Obey the safety instructions of the drive. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur.
[p205.b8] Note: Slot 2 in frames R1…R5 is at UDC potential. You must disconnect power supplies before installing or removing an I/O extension module.
[p205.b9] Stop the drive and do the steps in section Electrical safety precautions (page 22) before you start the work.
[p205.b10] (step 1) 1. Remove the front cover(s) if not already removed. See section Connection procedure, frames R1…R4 (page 174), section Connection procedure, frame R5 (page 178) or section IP21 (UL Type 1) (page 81). The figures for frames R1…R5 and R6…R9 show an example of installing option modules.
[p205.b11] Option slot 2 (I/O extension modules)
[p205.b12] (step 2) 2. Frame R1 only: Install the option mounting.
[p205.b13] (step 3) 3. Put the module carefully into its position on the control unit.
[p205.b14] (step 4) 4. Tighten the mounting screw.
[p205.b15] (step 5) 5. Tighten the grounding screw (CHASSIS).
[p205.b16] Note: The screw grounds the module. It is necessary for fulfilling the EMC requirements and for proper operation of the module.
[p205.b17] Note: Frame R1: The module in option slot 2 covers the power terminals. Do not install a module in option slot 2 before you have installed the power cables.
[p205.b18] Option slot 1 (fieldbus adapter modules)
[p205.b19] (step 6) 6. Put the module carefully into its position on the control unit.
[p205.b20] (step 7) 7. Tighten the mounting screw (CHASSIS).
[p205.b21] Note: The screw tightens the connections and grounds the module. It is necessary for fulfilling the EMC requirements and for proper operation of the module.

[p212.b2] Connecting a PC

[p212.b9] (step 3) 3. Connect an USB cable (Type A to Type Mini-B) between the USB connector on the control panel (3a) and a free USB port on the PC (3b).
[p212.b10] (step 4) 4. The panel will display an indication whenever the connection is active.
[p212.b11] (step 5) 5. See the documentation of the PC tool for setup instructions.
