[p213.b1] Installation checklist 209
[p213.b2] 8
[p213.b3] Installation checklist
[p213.b4] Contents of this chapter
[p213.b5] This chapter contains a checklist of the mechanical and electrical installation of the drive.
[p213.b6] Checklist
[p213.b7] Examine the mechanical and electrical installation of the drive before start-up. Go through the checklist together with another person.
[p213.b8] WARNING! Obey the safety instructions of the drive. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur. If you are not a qualified electrical professional, do not do installation, commissioning or maintenance work.
[p213.b9] WARNING! Stop the drive and do the steps in section Electrical safety precautions (page 22) before you start the work.
[p213.t1.r1] TABLE COLUMNS: Make sure that …
[p213.t1.r2] Make sure that …: The ambient operating conditions meet the drive ambient conditions specification and enclosure rating (IP code ).
[p213.t1.r3] Make sure that …: The supply voltage matches the nominal input voltage of the drive. See the type designation label.
=== page 214 ===
[p214.b1] 210 Installation checklist
[p214.t1.r1] TABLE COLUMNS: Make sure that …
[p214.t1.r2] Make sure that …: The insulation resistance of the input power cable, motor cable and motor is measured according to local regulations and the manuals of the drive.
[p214.t1.r3] Make sure that …: The drive is attached securely on an even, vertical and non-flammable wall.
[p214.t1.r4] Make sure that …: The cooling air flows freely in and out of the drive.
[p214.t1.r5] Make sure that …: If the drive is connected to a network other than a symmetrically grounded TN-S system: You have done all the required modifications (for example, you may need to disconnect the EMC filter or ground-to-phase varistor). See the electrical installation instructions.
[p214.t1.r6] Make sure that …: Appropriate AC fuses and main disconnecting device are installed.
[p214.t1.r7] Make sure that …: There is an adequately sized protective earth (ground) conductor(s) between the drive and the switchboard, the conductor is connected to correct terminal, and the terminal is tightened to the correct torque. Proper grounding has also been measured according to the regulations.
[p214.t1.r8] Make sure that …: The input power cable is connected to the correct terminals, the phase order is correct, and the terminals are tightened to the correct torque.
[p214.t1.r9] Make sure that …: There is an adequately sized protective earth (ground) conductor between the motor and the drive, and the conductor is connected to the correct terminal, and the terminal is tightened to the correct torque. Proper grounding has also been measured according to the regulations.
[p214.t1.r10] Make sure that …: The motor cable is connected to the correct terminals, the phase order is correct, and the terminals are tightened to the correct torque.
[p214.t1.r11] Make sure that …: The motor cable is routed away from other cables.
[p214.t1.r12] Make sure that …: No power factor compensation capacitors are connected to the motor cable.
[p214.t1.r13] Make sure that …: If an external brake resistor is connected to the drive: There is an adequately sized pro- tective earth (ground) conductor between the brake resistor and the drive, and the con- ductor is connected to the correct terminal, and the terminals are tightened to the correct torque. Proper grounding has also been measured according to the regulations.
[p214.t1.r14] Make sure that …: If an external brake resistor is connected to the drive: The brake resistor cable is connected to the correct terminals, and the terminals are tightened to the correct torque.
[p214.t1.r15] Make sure that …: If an external brake resistor is connected to the drive: The brake resistor cable is routed away from other cables.
[p214.t1.r16] Make sure that …: The control cables are connected to the correct terminals, and the terminals are tightened to the correct torque.
[p214.t1.r17] Make sure that …: If a drive bypass connection will be used: The Direct On Line contactor of the motor and the drive output contactor are either mechanically and/or electrically interlocked, that is, they cannot be closed at the same time. A thermal overload device must be used for protection when bypassing the drive. Refer to local codes and regulations.
[p214.t1.r18] Make sure that …: There are no tools, foreign objects or dust from drilling inside the drive.
=== page 215 ===
[p215.b1] Installation checklist 211
[p215.t1.r1] TABLE COLUMNS: Make sure that …
[p215.t1.r2] Make sure that …: The area in front of the drive is clean: the drive cooling fan cannot draw any dust or dirt inside.
[p215.t1.r3] Make sure that …: Drive covers and cover of the motor connection box are in place.
[p215.t1.r4] Make sure that …: The motor and the driven equipment are ready for power-up.

=== page 219 ===
[p219.b1] Maintenance 215
[p219.b2] Note:
[p219.b3] • Maintenance and component replacement intervals are based on the assumption that the equipment is operated within the specified ratings and ambient conditions. ABB recommends annual drive inspections to ensure the highest reliability and optimum performance.
[p219.b4] • Long term operation near the specified maximum ratings or ambient conditions may require shorter maintenance intervals for certain components. Consult your local ABB Service representative for additional maintenance recommendations.
[p219.b5] Cleaning the exterior of the drive
[p219.b6] WARNING! Obey the safety instructions of the drive. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur. If you are not a qualified electrical professional, do not do installation, commissioning or maintenance work.
[p219.b7] (step 1) 1. Stop the drive and do the steps in section Electrical safety precautions (page 22) before you start the work.
[p219.b8] (step 2) 2. Clean the exterior of the drive. Use:
[p219.b9] • vacuum cleaner with an antistatic hose and nozzle
[p219.b10] • soft brush
[p219.b11] • dry or damp (not wet) cleaning cloth. Moisten with clean water, or mild detergent (pH 5-9 for metal, pH 5-7 for plastic).
[p219.b12] WARNING! Prevent water from entering the drive. Never use excessive amount of water, a hose, steam, etc.
=== page 220 ===
[p220.b1] 216 Maintenance
[p220.b2] Cleaning the heatsink
[p220.b3] The drive module heatsink fins pick up dust from the cooling air. The drive runs into overtemperature warnings and faults if the heatsink is not clean. When necessary, clean the heatsink as follows.
[p220.b4] WARNING! Use the required personal protective equipment. Wear protective gloves and long sleeves. Some parts have sharp edges.
[p220.b5] WARNING! Use a vacuum cleaner with antistatic hose and nozzle, and wear a grounding wristband. Using a normal vacuum cleaner creates static discharges which can damage circuit boards.
[p220.b6] (step 1) 1. Stop the drive and do the steps in section Electrical safety precautions (page 22) before you start the work.
[p220.b7] (step 2) 2. Remove the module cooling fan(s). See the separate instructions.
[p220.b8] (step 3) 3. Blow dry, clean and oil-free compressed air from bottom to top and simultaneously use a vacuum cleaner at the air outlet to trap the dust. If there is a risk of dust entering adjoining equipment, do the cleaning in another room.
[p220.b9] (step 4) 4. Reinstall the cooling fan.
=== page 221 ===
[p221.b1] Maintenance 217
[p221.b2] Fans
[p221.b3] See Maintenance intervals (page 213) for the fan replacement interval in average operation conditions.
[p221.b4] Parameter 05.04 Fan on-time counter indicates the running time of the cooling fan. Reset the counter after a fan replacement. See the firmware manual.
[p221.b5] In a speed-controlled fan, the speed of the fan matches the cooling needs. This increases the life span of the fan.
[p221.b6] Main fans are speed controlled. When the drive is stopped, the main fan runs at low speed until the drive cools down. IP21 (UL Type 1) frames R5…R9 and all IP55 (UL Type 12) frames have auxiliary fans that are not speed controlled and run all the time when the control unit is powered.
[p221.b7] Replacement fans are available from the manufacturer. Do not use other than specified spare parts.

[p231.b1] Maintenance 227
[p231.b2] Capacitors
[p231.b3] The DC link of the drive contains several electrolytic capacitors. Operating time, load, and surrounding air temperature have an effect on the life of the capacitors. Capacitor life can be extended by decreasing the surrounding air temperature.
[p231.b4] Capacitor failure is usually followed by damage to the unit and an input cable fuse failure, or a fault trip. If you think that any capacitors in the drive have failed, contact ABB.
[p231.b5] ￭Reforming the capacitors
[p231.b6] The capacitors must be reformed if the drive has not been powered (either in storage or unused) for a year or more. The manufacturing date is on the type designation label. For information on reforming the capacitors, see Capacitor reforming instructions (3BFE64059629 [English]) in the ABB Library (https://library.abb.com/en).
[p231.b7] Control panel
[p231.b8] See ACS-AP-I, -S, -W and ACH-AP-H, -W assistant control panels user’s manual (3AUA0000085685 [English]).
[p231.b9] LEDs
[p231.b10] ￭Drive LEDs
[p231.b11] There is a green POWER and a red FAULT LED on the front of the drive. They are visible through the panel cover but invisible if a control panel is attached to the drive. The table below describes the drive LED indications.
[p231.t1.r1] column 1: Drive LEDs POWER and FAULT, on the front of the drive, under the control panel / panel cover If a control panel is attached to the drive, switch to remote control (otherwise a fault will be generated), and then remove the panel to be able to see the LEDs

=== page 233 ===
[p233.b1] Maintenance 229
[p233.b2] Functional safety components
[p233.b3] The mission time of functional safety components is 20 years which equals the time during which failure rates of electronic components remain constant. This applies to the components of the standard Safe torque off circuit as well as any modules, relays and, typically, any other components that are part of functional safety circuits.
[p233.b4] The expiry of mission time terminates the certification and SIL/PL classification of the safety function. The following options exist:
[p233.b5] • Renewal of the whole drive and all optional functional safety module(s) and components.
[p233.b6] • Renewal of the components in the safety function circuit. In practice, this is economical only with larger drives that have replaceable circuit boards and other components such as relays.
[p233.b7] Note that some of the components may already have been renewed earlier, restarting their mission time. The remaining mission time of the whole circuit is however determined by its oldest component.
[p233.b8] Contact your local ABB service representative for more information.

[p242.b10] Definitions
[p242.b11] Nominal output voltage of the drive. For input voltage range [U1, see section Electrical power network specification (page 286). 50 Hz for IEC ratings and Un
[p242.b12] 60 Hz for UL (NEC) ratings.
[p242.b13] Nominal input current (rms) at 40 °C (104 °F). I1
[p242.b14] Maximum output current. Available for two seconds at start. Imax
[p242.b15] Maximum current with 10% overload, allowed for one minute every ten minutes. ILd
[p242.b16] Typical motor power in light-duty use (10% overload). The horsepower (hp) PLd [p242.b17] ratings apply to most NEMA 4-pole motors.
[p242.b18] Maximum current with 50% overload, allowed for one minute every ten minutes. IHd 1) Maximum current with 40% overload, allowed for one minute every ten minutes.
[p242.b19] Typical motor power in heavy-duty use (50% overload). PHd

[p244.b1] 240 Technical data
[p244.b2] ￭Sizing
[p244.b3] Drive sizing is based on the rated motor current, voltage and power. To achieve the rated motor power given in the table, the rated current of the drive must be higher than or equal to the rated motor current. Also the rated power of the drive must be higher than or equal to the rated motor power. The power ratings are the same regardless of the supply voltage within one voltage range.
[p244.b4] Note: The ratings apply at ambient temperature of 40 °C (104 °F) for I2 (ILd for UL (NEC)). Above theses temperatures derating is required.
[p244.b5] Note: The DriveSize dimensioning PC tool available from ABB (http://new.abb.com/drives/software-tools/drivesize) is recommended for selecting the drive, motor and gear combination.
[p244.b6] ￭Deratings
[p244.b7] The output load capacity (I2, ILd, IHd; note that Imax is not derated) decreases in certain situations. In situations, where full motor power is required, oversize the drive so that the total derated output current provides sufficient capacity to supply the required nominal voltage to run the motor.
[p244.b8] Note: The DriveSize dimensioning PC tool available from ABB (http://new.abb.com/drives/software-tools/drivesize) is also suitable for derating.
[p244.b9] Note: If several situations are present at a time, the effects of derating are cumulative:
[p244.b10] I2 (derated) or ILd (derated) or IHd (derated) = (I2 or ILd or IHd) x (switching frequency derating) x (altitude derating) x (ambient temperature derating), where no derating = 1.0.
[p244.b11] Note: The motor may have a derating on it too.
[p244.b12] Example 1, IEC: How to calculate the derated current
[p244.b13] The IP21 / UL Type 1 drive type is ACS580-01-01-062A-4, which has drive output current of 62 A. Calculate the derated drive output current (I2) at 4kHz switching frequency, at 1500 m altitude and at 50 °C ambient temperature as follows:
[p244.b14] (step 1) 1. Switching frequency derating by derating factor (page 246): No derating needed for 4 kHz.
[p244.b15] (step 2) 2. Altitude derating (page 245): The derating factor for 1500 m is 1 - 1/10 000 m · (1500 - 1000) m = 0.95. The derated drive output current becomes I2 = 0.95 · 62 A = 58.9 A.
[p244.b16] (step 3) 3. Surrounding air temperature derating, IP21 (UL Type 1) (page 242): The derating factor for 50 °C ambient temperature = 0.90. The derated drive output current becomes then I2 = 0.90 · 58.9 A = 53.01 A.
[p244.b17] Example 1, UL (NEC): How to calculate the derated current
=== page 245 ===
[p245.b1] Technical data 241
[p245.b2] The IP21 / UL Type 1 drive type is ACS580-01-01-052A-4, which has drive output current of 52 A. Calculate the derated drive output current (ILd) at 4kHz switching frequency, at 4921 ft (1500 m) altitude and at 50 °C ambient temperature as follows:
[p245.b3] (step 1) 1. Switching frequency derating by derating factor (page 246): No derating needed for 4 kHz.
[p245.b4] (step 2) 2. Altitude derating (page 245): The derating factor for 4921 ft (1500 m) is 1 - 1/10 000 m · (1500 - 1000) m = 0.95. The derated drive output current becomes ILd = 0.95 · 52 A = 49.4 A.
[p245.b5] (step 3) 3. Surrounding air temperature derating, IP21 (UL Type 1) (page 242): The derating factor for 50 °C ambient temperature = 0.90. The derated drive output current becomes then ILd = 0.90 · 49.4 A = 44.46 A.
[p245.b6] Example 2, IEC: How to calculate the required drive
[p245.b7] If your application requires continuous 12.0 A of motor current (I2) at 8 kHz switching frequency, the supply voltage is 400 V and the drive is situated at 1500 m altitude and at 35 °C ambient temperature, calculate the appropriate IP21 / (UL Type 1) drive size requirement as follows:
[p245.b8] (step 1) 1. Switching frequency derating by derating factor (page 246): The minimum size required is I2 = 12.0 A / 0.65 = 18.46 A, where 0.65 is the derating for 8 kHz switching frequency (frames R2…R3).
[p245.b9] (step 2) 2. Altitude derating (page 245): The derating factor for 1500 m is 1 - 1/10 000 m · (1500 - 1000) m = 0.95. The minimum size required becomes then I2 = 18.46 A / 0.95 = 19.43 A.
[p245.b10] (step 3) 3. Surrounding air temperature derating, IP21 (UL Type 1) (page 242): No derating needed for 35 °C ambient temperature.
[p245.b11] Referring to I2 in the ratings tables (starting from page 232), drive type ACS580-01-01-026A-4 exceeds the I2 requirement of 19.43 A.
[p245.b12] Example 2, UL (NEC): How to calculate the required drive
[p245.b13] If your application requires continuous maximum current with 10% overload 12.0 A of motor current (ILd) at 8 kHz switching frequency, the supply voltage is 480 V and the drive is situated at 4921 ft (1500 m) altitude and at 35 °C ambient temperature, calculate the appropriate IP21 / UL Type 1 drive size requirement as follows:
[p245.b14] (step 1) 1. Switching frequency derating by derating factor (page 246): The minimum size required is ILd = 12.0 A / 0.65 = 18.46 A, where 0.65 is the derating for 8 kHz switching frequency (frames R2…R3).
[p245.b15] (step 2) 2. Altitude derating (page 245): The derating factor for 4921 ft (1500 m) is 1 - 1/10 000 m · (1500 - 1000) m = 0.95. The minimum size required becomes then ILd = 18.46 A / 0.95 = 19.43 A.

[p249.b14] Altitude derating
[p249.b15] In altitudes 1000…4000 m (3300…13120 ft) above sea level, the derating is 1% for every 100 m (330 ft).
[p249.b16] Note: There are special considerations in corner-grounded installations above 2000 m. Contact your local ABB representative for further information.
[p249.b17] The output current is calculated by multiplying the current given in the rating table by the derating factor k, which for x meters (1000 m <= x <= 4000 m) is:
[p249.b18] Altitude and surrounding air temperature
[p249.b19] At altitudes from 1000…4000 m (3281…13123 ft) above sea level and temperature +40 °C (+104 °F), the derating is 1 percentage point for every additional 100 m (328 ft).
[p249.b20] If surrounding air temperature is below +40 °C, the derating can be reduced by 1.5 percentage point for every 1 °C reduction in temperature.
[p249.b21] A few combined altitude and temperature derating curves for 1000…4000 m are shown below. For example, if the temperature is 30 °C, the derating factor is 1 - 1.5% · 10 = 0.85.
[p249.b22] For a more accurate derating, use the DriveSize PC tool.

[p257.b11] Output frequency derating
[p257.b12] Output frequency derating applies for ratings up to ACS580-01-106A-4 (R5). Inverter output current is limited by the following factor k below 5 Hz absolute inverter output frequency f_abs.
[p257.b13] k = 2/3 + 1/3 · (f_abs / 5 Hz)
[p257.b14] Fuses (IEC)
[p257.b15] gG as well as uR or aR fuses for protection against short-circuit in the input power cable or drive are listed below. Either fuse type can be used for frames R1…R9 if it operates rapidly enough. The operating time depends on the supply network impedance and the cross-sectional area and length of the supply cable.
[p257.b16] Note 1: See also Implementing short-circuit and thermal overload protection (page 104).
[p257.b17] Note 2: Fuses with higher current rating than the recommended ones must not be used.
[p257.b18] Note 3: Fuses from other manufacturers can be used if they meet the ratings and the melting curve of the fuse does not exceed the melting curve of the fuse mentioned in the table.
[p257.b19] ￭gG fuses
[p257.b20] Check on the fuse time-current curve to ensure the operating time of the fuse is below 0.5 seconds. Obey the local regulations.

[p261.b19] Circuit breakers (IEC)
[p261.b20] This section does not apply to the North American market. See section Circuit breakers (UL).
[p261.b21] The protective characteristics of circuit breakers depend on the type, construction and settings of the breakers. There are also limitations pertaining to the short-circuit capacity of the supply network.
[p261.b22] WARNING! Due to the inherent operating principle and construction of circuit breakers, independent of the manufacturer, hot ionized gases can escape from the breaker enclosure in case of a short-circuit. To make sure of safe use, pay special attention to the installation and placement of the breakers. Obey the manufacturer’s instructions.
[p261.b23] You can use the circuit breakers listed below. Other circuit breakers can be used with drive if they provide the same electrical characteristics. ABB does not assume any liability whatsoever for the correct function and protection with circuit breakers not listed below. Furthermore, if the recommendations given by ABB are not obeyed, the drive can experience problems that the warranty does not cover.

[p264.b33] (step 1) 1) Class J, CC, and CF fuses are also allowed at the same nominal current and voltage ratings 2) See note 8 below
[p264.b34] (step 1) 1. Fuses are required as part of the installation, are not included in the base drive configuration and must be provided by others.
[p264.b35] (step 2) 2. Fuses with a higher current rating than specified must not be used.
=== page 265 ===
[p265.b1] Technical data 261
[p265.b2] (step 3) 3. The UL listed fuses recommended by ABB are the required branch circuit protection per NEC. Circuit breakers listed in section Circuit breakers (UL) are also acceptable as branch circuit protection.
[p265.b3] (step 4) 4. The recommended size or smaller UL listed 248 fast acting, time delay, or high speed fuses must be used to maintain the UL listing of the drive. Additional protection can be used. Refer to local codes and regulations.
[p265.b4] (step 5) 5. A fuse of a different class can be used at the high fault rating where the Ipeak and I2t of the new fuse is not greater than that of the specified fuse.
[p265.b5] (step 6) 6. UL listed 248 fast acting, time delay, or high speed fuses from other manufacturers can be used if they meet the same class and rating requirements specified in the rules above.
[p265.b6] (step 7) 7. When installing a drive, always follow ABB installation instructions, NEC requirements and local codes.
[p265.b7] (step 8) 8. Only 480 V R9 drives with serial numbers beginning 1204109256 when built in Finland and beginning 22106xxxxx when built in the U.S. may be protected with fuses other than Class T fuses.
[p265.b8] (step 9) 9. Alternative fuses can be used if they meet certain characteristics. For acceptable fuses, see the manual supplement (3AXD50000645015).
[p265.b9] Circuit breakers (UL)
[p265.b10] These drives are suitable for use on a circuit capable of delivering not more than 65 kA symmetrical amperes (RMS) at 240 / 480 / 600 V maximum, when protected by appropriate circuit breakers in the tables below. Additional fuse protection is not required by UL when using circuit breakers herein. Circuit breakers are not required to be in the same enclosure as the drive.
[p265.b11] Notes below the tables must be followed when using these breakers.

[p267.b38] Notes:
=== page 268 ===
[p268.b1] 264 Technical data
[p268.b2] (step 1) 1. Drives that have an enclosure minimum volume listed must be mounted in an enclosure ≥enclosure minimum volume specified in the tables above.
[p268.b3] (step 2) 2. When multiple drives that have an enclosure minimum volume specified are installed in the same enclosure, minimum volume of the enclosure is determined by largest enclosure minimum volume of the drives to be placed in the enclosure, plus the volume(s) of each additional drive. i.e. for the 480V R6 and R3 drive select enclosure with the volume ≥53703+1011 = 54714 in3.
[p268.b4] (step 3) 3. For UL Open Type, UL Type 1 or UL Type 12 drives that have a minimum enclosure volume indicated with ¤, no minimum enclosure volume is required but the drive must be mounted inside an enclosure.
[p268.b5] (step 4) 4. If combining a drive with an enclosure minimum volume specified and others with an enclosure minimum volume indicated with ¤, start with the largest specified enclosure minimum volume listed and add the drive volumes for the other drives.
[p268.b6] (step 5) 5. If you are only mounting drives with no enclosure minimum volume specified, you have no restrictions on the enclosure size, but follow air clearances specified in the drive HW manuals for sufficient ventilation around each drive.
[p268.b7] (step 6) 6. UL Open Type, UL Type 1 and UL Type 12 drives can be used inside of the enclosure. Use drive volume for all three types listed in the table when installing multiple drives in the enclosure.
[p268.b8] (step 7) 7. The ABB circuit breaker part number listed in the table is a base part number.
[p268.b9] • Symbol α represents 80% or 100% allowable continuous current. Options allowed are U, Q, C and D.
[p268.b10] • Symbol β represents the number of poles for the breaker. Options allowed are 3, and 4.
[p268.b11] • Symbol # represents trip units. Trip units allowed include A thru C, E thru L, P thru Z. If using Ekip breakers, set the overload current of the circuit breaker equal to or less than the value shown in the “CB Maximum Current” column in the tables above.
[p268.b12] • The digits indicated with an “*” represent accessories for the breakers and have no impact on the drive UL listing or performance or rating of the breaker.
[p268.b13] • For the ABB circuit breaker configurator refer to: https://lowvoltageconfigurator. tnb.com/configurator/#/config/tmax_xt
[p268.b14] (step 8) 8. Ratings in the tables are maximum for the given circuit breaker frame size. Breakers of the same frame size and interrupting rating with lower current ratings are also allowed.
[p268.b15] (step 9) 9. Using a circuit breaker with a lower KAIC rating is not allowed even if the available SC current is less than 65kA. 230V drives were tested with ABB inverse time circuit breakers rated at 65kA and 240V.
=== page 269 ===
[p269.b1] Technical data 265
[p269.b2] Notes 10 and 11 for 230V drives only:
[p269.b3] (step 10) 10. Other manufacturers' inverse time circuit breakers can be used if they are UL 489 listed, they are 240V or higher, they have a 65kA or higher interrupting rating and they have the same or lower nominal current rating than the ABB specified circuit breaker.
[p269.b4] (step 11) 11. Current limiting inverse time circuit breakers must not be used. 480V and 600V drives were tested with ABB current limiting inverse time circuit breakers rated at 65kA and 480V or 600V. Notes 12 and 13 for 480V and 600V drives only:
[p269.b5] (step 12) 12. When designing UL508A panels, Article SB 4.2.3 Exception No. 3 allows the use of other manufacturers' current limiting inverse time circuit breakers which have same voltage, current and interrupting rating, if Ipeak and I2t are the same or less than the ABB specified circuit breaker.
[p269.b6] (step 13) 13. Non-current limiting inverse time circuit breakers must not be used. Notes 14…16 for 480V drives only:
[p269.b7] (step 14) 14. Enclosures for frames R1, R3, and R9 must have a solid bottom directly below the drive. i.e. fans, filters or louvers cannot be mounted directly below the drive but can be mounted in adjacent areas on the bottom of the enclosure.
[p269.b8] (step 15) 15. Only 480V R8 frame drives with serial numbers after 1204301926 when built in Finland and after 2205002140 when built in the U.S. may be protected with circuit breakers listed in the tables above.
[p269.b9] (step 16) 16. Only 480V R9 frame drives with serial numbers beginning 1204109256 when built in Finland and beginning 22106xxxxx when built in the U.S. may be protected with circuit breakers listed in the tables above. Note 17 for 600V drives only:
[p269.b10] (step 17) 17. Enclosures for frames R2, R3, R5 and R9 must have a solid bottom directly below the drive. i.e. fans, filters or louvers cannot be mounted directly below the drive but can be mounted in adjacent areas on the bottom of the enclosure.
[p269.b11] (step 18) 18. Alternative circuit breakers can be used if they meet certain characteristics. For acceptable breakers see the manual supplement (3AXD50000645015 [English]).

[p275.b1] Technical data 271
[p275.b2] Note:
[p275.b3] (step 1) 1. For the actual degree of protection that can be achieved with flange for each frame size (on the back and front sides of the drive), see Flange mounting kit installation supplement (3AXD50000019100 [English]).
[p275.b4] (step 2) 2. Regarding flange mounting:
[p275.b5] • The outside of the cabinet sets the limit for vertical positioning, since that is where the cooling is required
[p275.b6] • There are no limitations inside the cabinet; practically the outside positioning defines the distance between drives
[p275.b7] • The space inside the cabinet can be used as long as the following requirements are still met:
[p275.b8] • Heat loss dissipation inside the cabinet per the hardware manual
[p275.b9] • Sufficient space for the maintenance operations
[p275.b10] • Wire bending radius rules according to UL when planning routing for mains and motor cables.

[p277.b4] Losses, cooling data and noise
[p277.b5] The air flow direction is from bottom to top.
[p277.b6] ￭Cooling air flow, heat dissipation and noise for stand-alone drives
[p277.b7] The table below specifies the heat dissipation in the main circuit at nominal load and in the control circuit with minimum load (I/O, options and panel not in use) and maximum load (all digital inputs and relays in the ON state, and the panel, fieldbus and fan in use). The total heat dissipation is the sum of the heat dissipation in the main and control circuits. Use the maximum heat dissipation when designing cabinet or electrical room cooling needs.

[p288.b18] (step 1) 1) The cable sizing is based on max. 6 cables laid on a cable ladder side by side, ambient temperature 30 °C, PVC insulation, surface temperature 70 °C (EN 60204-1 and IEC 60364- 5-52/2001). For other conditions, size the cables according to local safety regulations, appropriate input voltage and the load current of the drive. See page 278 for the accepted cable sizes of the drive. 2) Aluminum cables can be used with Un = 230 V frames R5…R8 only.
[p288.b19] Temperature: For IEC, select a cable rated for at least 70 °C maximum permissible temperature of conductor in continuous use. For North America, power cables must be rated for 90 °C (194 °F) or higher.
[p288.b20] Note: For drives with option +B056 (IP55, UL Type 12), select a cable rated for at least 90 °C (194 °F) maximum permissible temperature of conductor in continuous use.
[p288.b21] Voltage: 600 V AC cable is accepted for up to 500 V AC.

[p290.b25] Voltage (U1)
[p290.b26] • ACS580-01-xxxx-2 drives: Input voltage range 3~ 208…240 V AC +10%…. -15%. IEC: This is indicated in the type designation label as typical input voltage levels 3~ 230 V AC. North America: This is indicated in the type designation label as typical input voltage levels 1~ 208/230 V AC and 3~ 208/230 V AC. • ACS580-01-xxxx-4 drives: Input voltage range 3~ 380…480 V AC +10%…-15%. This is indicated in the type designation label as typical input voltage levels 3~ 400/480 V AC. • ACS580-01-xxxx-6 drives: Input voltage range 3~ 525…600 V AC +10%…-15%. This is indicated in the type designation label as typical input voltage level 3~ 600 V AC.
=== page 291 ===
[p291.b1] Technical data 287
[p291.b2] Network type
[p291.b3] Public low voltage networks. Symmetrically grounded TN-S system, IT (ungrounded), corner-grounded delta, midpoint- grounded delta and TT systems, see sections:
[p291.b4] IEC: When to disconnect EMC filter or ground-to-phase varistor: TN-S, IT, corner-grounded delta and midpoint-grounded delta systems (page 116) and Guidelines for installing the drive to a TT system (page 117). North America: When to connect EMC filter or disconnect ground-to-phase varistor: TN-S, IT, corner-grounded delta and midpoint-grounded delta systems (page 166) and Guidelines for installing the drive to a TT system (page 168).
[p291.b5] Note: Frames R4 and R5 cannot be used in corner-grounded or midpoint-grounded delta systems. 65 kA when protected by fuses given in the fuse tables Rated conditional short-circuit current (IEC 61800-5-1)
[p291.b6] Short-circuit current protection (UL 61800-5-1)
[p291.b7] US and Canada: The drive is suitable for use on a circuit cap- able of delivering not more than 100 kA symmetrical amperes (rms) at 480 V maximum when protected by fuses given in the fuse table.
[p291.b8] US and Canada: The drive is suitable for use on a circuit cap- able of delivering not more than 65 kA symmetrical amperes (RMS) maximum when protected by circuit breakers given in the circuit breaker table. 47 to 63 Hz. This is indicated in the type designation label as typical input frequency level f1 (50/60 Hz). Frequency (f1)

[p303.b6] Disposal
[p303.b7] The main parts of the drive can be recycled to preserve natural re- sources and energy. Product parts and materials should be dis- mantled and separated.
[p303.b8] Generally all metals, such as steel, aluminum, copper and its alloys, and precious metals can be recycled as material. Plastics, rubber, cardboard and other packaging material can be used in energy re- covery. Printed circuit boards and large electrolytic capacitors need selective treatment according to IEC 62635 guidelines. To aid recyc- ling, plastic parts are marked with an appropriate identification code. Contact your local ABB distributor for further information on environ- mental aspects and recycling instructions for professional recyclers. End of life treatment must follow international and local regulations.
[p303.b9] Applicable standards
[p303.b10] The drive complies with the following standards. The compliance with the European Low Voltage Directive is verified according to standard EN 61800-5-1.

[p303.b18] This drive complies with the standard provided that the short-circuit power Ssc is greater than or equal to the minimum short-circuit power given for the drive (listed for each drive type on page 302) at the interface point between the user's supply and the public system. [p307.b3] CE marking
[p307.b4] A CE mark is attached to the drive to verify that the drive follows the provisions of the European Low Voltage, EMC and RoHS Directives.The CE marking also verifies that the drive, in regard to its safety functions (such as Safe torque off), conforms with the Machinery Directive as a safety component.
[p307.b5] ￭Compliance with the European Low Voltage Directive
[p307.b6] The compliance with the European Low Voltage Directive has been verified according to standard EN 61800-5-1:2007. The declaration of conformity (3AXD10000302784) is available on the Internet. See section Document library on the Internet on the inside of the back cover.
[p307.b7] ￭Compliance with the European EMC Directive
[p307.b8] The EMC Directive defines the requirements for immunity and emissions of electrical equipment used within the European Union. The EMC product standard (EN 61800- 3:2004 + A1:2012) covers requirements stated for drives. See section Compliance with the EN 61800-3:2004 + A1:2012 below. The declaration of conformity (3AXD10000302784) is available on the Internet. See section Document library on the Internet on the inside of the back cover.
[p307.b9] ￭Compliance with the European ROHS II Directive 2011/65/EU
[p307.b10] The RoHS II Directive defines the restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment. The declaration of conformity (3AXD10000302784) is available on the Internet. See section Document library on the Internet on the inside of the back cover.
[p307.b11] ￭Compliance with the European WEEE Directive 2002/96/EC
[p307.b12] The WEEE Directive defines the regulated disposal and recycling of electric and electrical equipment.
=== page 308 ===
[p308.b1] 304 Technical data
[p308.b2] ￭Compliance with the European Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC 2nd Edition – June 2010
[p308.b3] The drive is a machinery component that can be integrated into a wide range of machinery categories as specified in European Commission’s Guide to application of the Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC 2nd Edition – June 2010. See chapter The Safe torque off function (page 347).
[p308.b4] Validating the operation of the Safe torque off function
[p308.b5] See chapter The Safe torque off function (page 347).
[p308.b6] Compliance with the EN 61800-3:2004 + A1:2012
[p308.b7] ￭Definitions
[p308.b8] EMC stands for Electromagnetic Compatibility. It is the ability of electrical/electronic equipment to operate without problems within an electromagnetic environment. Likewise, the equipment must not disturb or interfere with any other product or system within its locality.
[p308.b9] First environment includes establishments connected to a low-voltage network which supplies buildings used for domestic purposes.
[p308.b10] Second environment includes establishments connected to a network not supplying domestic premises.
[p308.b11] Drive of category C1: drive of rated voltage less than 1000 V and intended for use in the first environment.
[p308.b12] Drive of category C2: drive of rated voltage less than 1000 V and intended to be installed and started up only by a professional when used in the first environment.
[p308.b13] Note: A professional is a person or organization having necessary skills in installing and/or starting up power drive systems, including their EMC aspects.
[p308.b14] Drive of category C3: drive of rated voltage less than 1000 V and intended for use in the second environment and not intended for use in the first environment.
[p308.b15] Drive of category C4: drive of rated voltage equal to or above 1000 V, or rated current equal to or above 400 A, or intended for use in complex systems in the second environment.
[p308.b16] ￭Category C1
[p308.b17] The emission limits are complied with the following provisions:
[p308.b18] (step 1) 1. The optional EMC C1 filter is selected according to the documentation and installed as specified in the EMC C1 filter manual. See Main switch and EMC C1 filter options (+F278, +F316, +E223) installation supplement for ACS580-01, ACH580-01 and ACQ580-01 frames R1 to R5 (3AXD50000155132 [Multilingual]).

[p311.b3] UL checklist
[p311.b4] WARNING! Operation of this drive requires detailed installation and operation instructions provided in the hardware and software manuals. The manuals are provided in electronic format in the drive package or on the Internet. Keep the manuals with the drive at all times. Hard copies of the manuals can be ordered through the manufacturer.
[p311.b5] • Make sure that the drive type designation label includes the applicable marking.
[p311.b6] • DANGER - Risk of electric shock. After disconnecting the input power, always wait for 5 minutes to let the intermediate circuit capacitors discharge before you start working on the drive, motor or motor cable.
[p311.b7] • The drive is to be used in a heated, indoor controlled environment. The drive must be installed in clean air according to the enclosure classification. Cooling air must be clean, free from corrosive materials and electrically conductive dust.
[p311.b8] • The maximum surrounding air temperature is 40 °C at rated output current. The output current is derated for 40…50 °C.
[p311.b9] Note: For cabinet-built drives, the maximum surrounding air temperature is 40 °C (104 °F).
[p311.b10] • The drive is suitable for use in a circuit capable of delivering not more than 100 kA rms symmetrical amperes, 600 V maximum when protected by the UL fuses given elsewhere in this chapter.
[p311.b11] • The drive is suitable for use in a circuit capable of delivering not more than 65 kA rms symmetrical amperes, 600 V maximum when protected by the UL circuit breakers given elsewhere in this chapter.
[p311.b12] • The cables located within the motor circuit must be rated for at least 75 °C in UL-compliant installations.
[p311.b13] • The input cable must be protected with fuses or circuit breakers. These protective devices provide branch circuit protection in accordance with the national regulations (National Electrical Code (NEC) or Canadian Electrical Code). Obey also any other applicable local or provincial codes. Suitable UL fuses are listed in section Fuses (UL) (page 259) and circuit breakers in section Circuit breakers (IEC) (page 257).

[p312.b4] • The drive overvoltage category according to IEC 60664-1 is III

[p341.b1] Resistor braking 337
[p341.b2] 12
[p341.b3] Resistor braking
[p341.b4] Contents of this chapter
[p341.b5] This chapter describes how to select, protect and wire brake choppers and resistors. The chapter also contains technical data.
[p341.b6] Operation principle and hardware description
[p341.b7] The brake chopper handles the energy generated by a decelerating motor. The chopper connects the brake resistor to the intermediate DC circuit whenever the voltage in the circuit exceeds the limit defined by the control program. Energy consumption by the resistor losses lowers the voltage until the resistor can be disconnected.
[p341.b8] For frame R1…R3 internal brake choppers and resistors, see below. For R4…R9 external brake choppers and resistors, see Resistor braking, frames R4…R9 (page 343).
[p341.b9] Resistor braking, frames R1…R3
[p341.b10] ￭Planning the braking system
[p341.b11] Selecting the brake resistor
[p341.b12] Frames R1…R3 have an built-in brake chopper as standard equipment. The brake resistor is selected using the table and equations presented in this section.
[p341.b13] (step 1) 1. Determine the required maximum braking power PRmax for the application. PRmax must be smaller than PBRmax given in the table on page 338 for the used drive type.
[p341.b14] (step 2) 2. Calculate resistance R with Equation 1.
[p341.b15] (step 3) 3. Calculate energy ERpulse with Equation 2.
=== page 342 ===
[p342.b1] 338 Resistor braking
[p342.b2] (step 4) 4. Select the resistor so that the following conditions are met:
[p342.b3] • The rated power of the resistor must be greater than or equal to PRmax.
[p342.b4] • Resistance R must be between Rmin and Rmax given in the table for the used drive type.
[p342.b5] • The resistor must be able to dissipate energy ERpulse during the braking cycle T.
[p342.b6] Equations for selecting the resistor:
[p342.b7] Eq. 1.
[p342.b8] ton
[p342.b9] PRmax
[p342.b10] PRave
[p342.b11] Eq. 2.
[p342.b12] T
[p342.b13] Eq. 3.
[p342.b14] For conversion, use 1 hp = 746 W.
[p342.b15] where
[p342.b16] = calculated brake resistor value (ohm). Make sure that: Rmin < R < Rmax. R
[p342.b17] = maximum power during the braking cycle (W) PRmax
[p342.b18] = average power during the braking cycle (W) PRave
[p342.b19] = energy conducted into the resistor during a single braking pulse (J) ERpulse
[p342.b20] = length of the braking pulse (s) ton
[p342.b21] = length of the braking cycle (s). T

[p344.b13] Symbols
[p344.b14] = minimum allowed brake resistor that can be connected to the brake chopper Rmin
[p344.b15] = maximum allowed brake resistor that allows PBRmax Rmax

[p344.b17] WARNING! Do not use a brake resistor with a resistance below the minimum value specified for the particular drive. The drive and the internal chopper are not able to handle the overcurrent caused by the low resistance.
[p344.b18] Selecting and routing the brake resistor cables
[p344.b19] Use a shielded cable with the conductor size specified in section Terminal and entry data for the power cables on page Terminal and entry data for the power cables (page 278).
[p344.b20] Minimizing electromagnetic interference
[p344.b21] Follow these rules in order to minimize electromagnetic interference caused by the rapid current changes in the resistor cables:
[p344.b22] • Install the cables away from other cable routes.
[p344.b23] • Avoid long parallel runs with other cables. The minimum parallel cabling separation distance should be 0.3 meters.
[p344.b24] • Cross the other cables at right angles.
[p344.b25] • Keep the cable as short as possible in order to minimize the radiated emissions and stress on chopper IGBTs. The longer the cable the higher the radiated emissions, inductive load and voltage peaks over the IGBT semiconductors of the brake chopper.
=== page 345 ===
[p345.b1] Resistor braking 341
[p345.b2] Note: ABB has not verified that the EMC requirements are fulfilled with external user-defined brake resistors and cabling. The EMC compliance of the complete installation must be considered by the customer.
[p345.b3] Maximum cable length
[p345.b4] The maximum length of the resistor cable(s) is 10 m (33 ft).
[p345.b5] Placing the brake resistor
[p345.b6] Install the resistors outside the drive in a place where they will cool.
[p345.b7] Arrange the cooling of the resistor in a way that:
[p345.b8] • no danger of overheating is caused to the resistor or nearby materials
[p345.b9] • the temperature of the room the resistor is located in does not exceed the allowed maximum.
[p345.b10] Supply the resistor with cooling air/water according to the resistor manufacturer’s instructions.
[p345.b11] WARNING! The materials near the brake resistor must be non-flammable. The surface temperature of the resistor is high. Air flowing from the resistor is of hundreds of degrees Celsius. If the exhaust vents are connected to a ventilation system, make sure that the material withstands high temperatures. Protect the resistor against contact.
[p345.b12] Protecting the system in brake circuit fault situations
[p345.b13] Protecting the system in cable and brake resistor short-circuit situations
[p345.b14] The drive input fuses will also protect the resistor cable when it is identical with the input power cable.
[p345.b15] Protecting the system against thermal overload
[p345.b16] The drive has a brake thermal model which protects the brake resistor against overload. ABB recommends to enable the thermal model at start up.
[p345.b17] ABB recommends to equip the drive with a main contactor for safety reasons even when you have enabled the resistor thermal model. Wire the contactor so that it opens in case the resistor overheats. This is essential for safety since the drive will not otherwise be able to interrupt the main supply if the chopper remains conductive in a fault situation. An example wiring diagram is shown below. ABB recommends that you use resistors equipped with a thermal switch (1) inside the resistor assembly. The switch indicates overtemperature.
=== page 346 ===
[p346.b1] 342 Resistor braking
[p346.b2] ABB recommends that you also wire the thermal switch to a digital input of the drive, and configure the input to cause a fault trip at resistor overtemperature indication.

=== page 347 ===
[p347.b1] Resistor braking 343
[p347.b2] Connect the thermal switch of the brake resistor as described in Protecting the system against thermal overload (page 341).
[p347.b3] ￭Start-up
[p347.b4] Start-up
[p347.b5] Note: New brake resistors may be coated with storage grease. As the brake chopper operates for the first time, the grease burns off and may produce some smoke. Make sure there is sufficient ventilation.
[p347.b6] Set the following parameters (HVAC control program):
[p347.b7] • Disable the overvoltage control of the drive by parameter 30.30 Overvoltage control.
[p347.b8] • Set parameter 31.01 External event 1 source to point to the digital input where the thermal switch of the brake resistor is wired.
[p347.b9] • Set parameter 31.02 External event 1 type to Fault.
[p347.b10] • Enable the brake chopper by parameter 43.06 Brake chopper enable. If Enabled with thermal model is selected, set also the brake resistor overload protection parameters 43.08 and 43.09 according to the application.
[p347.b11] • Check the resistance value of parameter 43.10 Brake resistance.
[p347.b12] With these parameter settings, the drive stops by coasting on brake resistor overtemperature.
[p347.b13] WARNING! If the drive is equipped with a brake chopper but the chopper is not enabled by the parameter setting, the internal thermal protection of the drive against resistor overheating is not in use. In this case, the brake resistor must be disconnected.
[p347.b14] Resistor braking, frames R4…R9
[p347.b15] ￭Planning the braking system
[p347.b16] Frames R4…R9 need external brake choppers and resistors. The table below lists suitable choppers and resistors.
[p347.b17] For more information, see NBRA-6xx Braking Choppers Installation and start-up guide (3AFY58920541 [English]) and ACS-BRK Brake Units Installation and start-up guide (3AFY61514309 [English]).

[p351.b1] The Safe torque off function 347
[p351.b2] 13
[p351.b3] The Safe torque off function
[p351.b4] Contents of this chapter
[p351.b5] This chapter describes the Safe torque off (STO) function of the drive and gives instructions for its use.
[p351.b6] Description
[p351.b7] The Safe torque off function can be used, for example, as the final actuator device of safety circuits that stop the drive in case of danger (such as an emergency stop circuit). Another typical application is a prevention of unexpected start-up function that enables short-time maintenance operations like cleaning or work on non-electrical parts of the machinery without switching off the power supply to the drive.
[p351.b8] When activated, the Safe torque off function disables the control voltage for the power semiconductors of the drive output stage (A, see the diagrams below), thus preventing the drive from generating the torque required to rotate the motor. If the motor is running when Safe torque off is activated, it coasts to a stop.
[p351.b9] The Safe torque off function has a redundant architecture, that is, both channels must be used in the safety function implementation. The safety data given in this manual is calculated for redundant use, and does not apply if both channels are not used.
[p351.b10] The Safe torque off function complies with these standards:
[p351.t1.r1] The Safe torque off function: Standard | complies with these standards:: Name
[p351.t1.r2] The Safe torque off function: IEC 60204-1:2016 EN 60204-1:2018 | complies with these standards:: Safety of machinery – Electrical equipment of machines – Part 1: General requirements
[p351.b11] Name Standard
[p351.b12] Safety of machinery – Electrical equipment of machines – Part 1: General requirements IEC 60204-1:2016 EN 60204-1:2018

=== page 358 ===
[p358.b1] 354 The Safe torque off function
[p358.b2] ￭Activation switch
[p358.b3] In the wiring diagrams, the activation switch has the designation [K]. This represents a component such as a manually operated switch, an emergency stop push button switch, or the contacts of a safety relay or safety PLC.
[p358.b4] • In case a manually operated activation switch is used, the switch must be of a type that can be locked out to the open position.
[p358.b5] • The contacts of the switch or relay must open/close within 200 ms of each other.
[p358.b6] • A CPTC-02 thermistor protection module can also be used. For more information, see the module documentation.
[p358.b7] ￭Cable types and lengths
[p358.b8] • Double-shielded twisted-pair cable is recommended.
[p358.b9] • Maximum cable lengths:
[p358.b10] • 300 m (1000 ft) between activation switch [K] and drive control unit
[p358.b11] • 60 m (200 ft) between multiple drives
[p358.b12] • 60 m (200 ft) between external power supply and first control unit
[p358.b13] Note: A short-circuit in the wiring between the switch and an STO terminal causes a dangerous fault. Therefore, it is recommended to use a safety relay (including wiring diagnostics) or a wiring method (shield grounding, channel separation) which reduces or eliminates the risk caused by the short-circuit.
[p358.b14] Note: The voltage at the STO input terminals of the drive must be at least 13 V DC to be interpreted as “1”. The pulse tolerance of the input channels is 1 ms.
[p358.b15] ￭Grounding of protective shields
[p358.b16] • Ground the shield in the cabling between the activation switch and the control unit at the control unit only.
[p358.b17] • Ground the shield in the cabling between two control units at one control unit only.
=== page 359 ===
[p359.b1] The Safe torque off function 355
[p359.b2] Operation principle
[p359.b3] (step 1) 1. The Safe torque off activates (the activation switch is opened, or safety relay contacts open).
[p359.b4] (step 2) 2. The STO inputs of the drive control unit de-energize.
[p359.b5] (step 3) 3. The control unit cuts off the control voltage from the output IGBTs.
[p359.b6] (step 4) 4. The control program generates an indication as defined by parameter 31.22 (see the firmware manual of the drive). The parameter selects which indications are given when one or both STO signals are switched off or lost. The indications also depend on whether the drive is running or stopped when this occurs.
[p359.b7] Note: This parameter does not affect the operation of the STO function itself. The STO function will operate regardless of the setting of this parameter: a running drive will stop upon removal of one or both STO signals, and will not start until both STO signals are restored and all faults reset.
[p359.b8] Note: The loss of only one STO signal always generates a fault as it is interpreted as a malfunction of STO hardware or wiring.
[p359.b9] (step 5) 5. The motor coasts to a stop (if running). The drive cannot restart while the activation switch or safety relay contacts are open. After the contacts close, a reset may be needed (depending on the setting of parameter 31.22). A new start command is required to start the drive.
=== page 360 ===
[p360.b1] 356 The Safe torque off function
[p360.b2] Start-up including validation test
[p360.b3] To ensure the safe operation of a safety function, validation is required. The final assembler of the machine must validate the function by performing a validation test. The test must be performed
[p360.b4] • at initial start-up of the safety function
[p360.b5] • after any changes related to the safety function (circuit boards, wiring, components, settings, etc.)
[p360.b6] • after any maintenance work related to the safety function
[p360.b7] • at the proof test of the safety function
[p360.b8] • after a drive firmware update.
[p360.b9] ￭Competence
[p360.b10] The validation test of the safety function must be carried out by a competent person with adequate expertise and knowledge of the safety function as well as functional safety, as required by IEC 61508-1 clause 6. The test procedures and report must be documented and signed by this person.
[p360.b11] ￭Validation test reports
[p360.b12] Signed validation test reports must be stored in the logbook of the machine. The report shall include documentation of start-up activities and test results, references to failure reports and resolution of failures. Any new validation tests performed due to changes or maintenance shall be logged into the logbook.
[p360.b13] ￭Validation test procedure
[p360.b14] After wiring the Safe torque off function, validate its operation as follows.
[p360.b15] Note: If a CPTC-02 module is installed, refer to its documentation.
[p360.t1.r1] column 1: Action
[p360.t1.r2] column 1: WARNING! Obey the safety instructions. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur.
[p360.t1.r3] column 1: Make sure that the drive can be run and stopped freely during start-up.
[p360.t1.r4] column 1: Stop the drive (if running), switch the input power off and isolate the drive from the power line using a disconnector.
[p360.t1.r5] column 1: Check the STO circuit connections against the wiring diagram.
[p360.t1.r6] column 1: Close the disconnector and switch the power on.
=== page 361 ===
[p361.b1] The Safe torque off function 357
[p361.t1.r1] TABLE COLUMNS: Action
[p361.t1.r2] Action: Test the operation of the STO function when the motor is stopped. • Give a stop command for the drive (if running) and wait until the motor shaft is at a standstill. Make sure that the drive operates as follows: • Open the STO circuit. The drive generates an indication if one is defined for the 'stopped' state in parameter 31.22 (see the firmware manual). • Give a start command to verify that the STO function blocks the drive's operation. The drive generates a warning. The motor should not start. • Close the STO circuit. • Reset any active faults. Restart the drive and check that the motor runs normally.
[p361.t1.r3] Action: Test the operation of the STO function when the motor is running. • Start the drive and make sure the motor is running. • Open the STO circuit. The motor should stop. The drive generates an indication if one is defined for the 'running' state in parameter 31.22 (see the firmware manual). • Reset any active faults and try to start the drive. • Make sure that the motor stays at a standstill and the drive operates as described above in testing the operation when the motor is stopped. • Close the STO circuit. • Reset any active faults. Restart the drive and check that the motor runs normally.
[p361.t1.r4] Action: Test the operation of the failure detection of the drive. The motor can be stopped or running. • Open the 1st channel of the STO circuit. If the motor was running, it should coast to a stop. The drive generates a FA81 Safe Torque Off 1 loss fault indication (see the firmware manual). • Give a start command to verify that the STO function blocks the drive's operation. The motor should not start. • Close the STO circuit. • Reset any active faults. Restart the drive and check that the motor runs normally. • Open the 2nd channel of the STO circuit. If the motor was running, it should coast to a stop. The drive generates a FA82 Safe Torque Off 2 loss fault indication (see the firmware manual). • Give a start command to verify that the STO function blocks the drive's operation. The motor should not start. • Close the STO circuit. • Reset any active faults. Restart the drive and check that the motor runs normally.
[p361.t1.r5] Action: Document and sign the validation test report which verifies that the safety function is safe and accepted for operation.
=== page 362 ===
[p362.b1] 358 The Safe torque off function
[p362.b2] Use
[p362.b3] (step 1) 1. Open the activation switch, or activate the safety functionality that is wired to the STO connection.
[p362.b4] (step 2) 2. The STO inputs on the drive control unit de-energize, and the control unit cuts off the control voltage from the output IGBTs.
[p362.b5] (step 3) 3. The control program generates an indication as defined by parameter 31.22 (see the firmware manual of the drive).
[p362.b6] (step 4) 4. The motor coasts to a stop (if running). The drive will not restart while the activation switch or safety relay contacts are open.
[p362.b7] (step 5) 5. Deactivate the STO by closing the activation switch, or resetting the safety functionality that is wired to the STO connection.
[p362.b8] (step 6) 6. Reset any faults before restarting.
[p362.b9] WARNING! The Safe torque off function does not disconnect the voltage of the main and auxiliary circuits from the drive. Therefore maintenance work on electrical parts of the drive or the motor can only be carried out after isolating the drive from the supply and all other voltage sources.
[p362.b10] WARNING! The drive cannot detect or memorize any changes in the STO circuitry when the drive control unit is not powered. If both STO circuits are closed and a level-type start signal is active when the power is restored, it is possible that the drive starts without a fresh start command. Take this into account in the risk assessment of the system.
[p362.b11] This is also valid when the drive is only powered by a CMOD-xx multifunction extension module.
[p362.b12] WARNING! (With permanent magnet or synchronous reluctance [SynRM] motors only)
[p362.b13] In case of a multiple IGBT power semiconductor failure, the drive can produce an alignment torque which maximally rotates the motor shaft by 180/p degrees (with permanent magnet motors) or 180/2p degrees (with synchronous reluctance [SynRM] motors) regardless of the activation of the Safe torque off function. p denotes the number of pole pairs.
[p362.b14] Notes:
[p362.b15] • If a running drive is stopped by using the Safe torque off function, the drive will cut off the motor supply voltage and the motor will coast to a stop. If this causes danger
=== page 363 ===
[p363.b1] The Safe torque off function 359 [p363.b2] or is not otherwise acceptable, stop the drive and machinery using the appropriate stop mode before activating the Safe torque off function.
[p363.b3] • The Safe torque off function overrides all other functions of the drive.
[p363.b4] • The Safe torque off function is ineffective against deliberate sabotage or misuse.
[p363.b5] • The Safe torque off function has been designed to reduce the recognized hazardous conditions. In spite of this, it is not always possible to eliminate all potential hazards. The assembler of the machine must inform the final user about the residual risks.
=== page 364 ===
[p364.b1] 360 The Safe torque off function
[p364.b2] Maintenance
[p364.b3] After the operation of the circuit is validated at start-up, the STO function shall be maintained by periodic proof testing. In high demand mode of operation, the maximum proof test interval is 20 years. In low demand mode of operation, the maximum proof test interval is 5 or 2 years; see section Safety data (page 362). It is assumed that all dangerous failures of the STO circuit are detected by the proof test. To perform the proof test, do the Validation test procedure (page 356).
[p364.b4] Note: See also the Recommendation of Use CNB/M/11.050 (published by the European co-ordination of Notified Bodies) concerning dual-channel safety-related systems with electromechanical outputs:
[p364.b5] • When the safety integrity requirement for the safety function is SIL 3 or PL e (cat. 3 or 4), the proof test for the function must be performed at least every month.
[p364.b6] • When the safety integrity requirement for the safety function is SIL 2 (HFT = 1) or PL d (cat. 3), the proof test for the function must be performed at least every 12 months.
[p364.b7] The STO function of the drive does not contain any electromechanical components.
[p364.b8] In addition to proof testing, it is a good practice to check the operation of the function when other maintenance procedures are carried out on the machinery.
[p364.b9] Include the Safe torque off operation test described above in the routine maintenance program of the machinery that the drive runs.
[p364.b10] If any wiring or component change is needed after start-up, or the parameters are restored, do the test given in section Validation test procedure (page 356).
[p364.b11] Use only spare parts approved by ABB.
[p364.b12] Record all maintenance and proof test activities in the machine logbook.
[p364.b13] ￭Competence
[p364.b14] The maintenance and proof test activities of the safety function must be carried out by a competent person with adequate expertise and knowledge of the safety function as well as functional safety, as required by IEC 61508-1 clause 6.
=== page 365 ===
[p365.b1] The Safe torque off function 361
[p365.b2] Fault tracing
[p365.b3] The indications given during the normal operation of the Safe torque off function are selected by drive control program parameter 31.22.
[p365.b4] The diagnostics of the Safe torque off function cross-compare the status of the two STO channels. In case the channels are not in the same state, a fault reaction function is performed and the drive trips on an “STO hardware failure” fault. An attempt to use the STO in a non-redundant manner, for example activating only one channel, will trigger the same reaction.
[p365.b5] See the firmware manual of the drive control program for the indications generated by the drive, and for details on directing fault and warning indications to an output on the control unit for external diagnostics.
[p365.b6] Any failures of the Safe torque off function must be reported to ABB.

=== page 367 ===
[p367.b1] The Safe torque off function 363
[p367.b2] • 32 °C board temperature at 2.0% of time
[p367.b3] • 60 °C board temperature at 1.5% of time
[p367.b4] • 85 °C board temperature at 2.3% of time.
[p367.b5] • The STO is a type A safety component as defined in IEC 61508-2.
[p367.b6] • Relevant failure modes:
[p367.b7] • The STO trips spuriously (safe failure)
[p367.b8] • The STO does not activate when requested
[p367.b9] • A fault exclusion on the failure mode “short circuit on printed circuit board” has been made (EN 13849-2, table D.5). The analysis is based on an assumption that one failure occurs at one time. No accumulated failures have been analyzed.
[p367.b10] • STO response times:
[p367.b11] • STO reaction time (shortest detectable break): 1 ms
[p367.b12] • STO response time: 2 ms (typical), 5 ms (maximum)
[p367.b13] • Fault detection time: Channels in different states for longer than 200 ms
[p367.b14] • Fault reaction time: Fault detection time + 10 ms
[p367.b15] • Indication delays:
[p367.b16] • STO fault indication (parameter 31.22) delay: < 500 ms
[p367.b17] • STO warning indication (parameter 31.22) delay: < 1000 ms

breviation: Cat. | Reference: EN ISO 13849-1 | Description: Classification of the safety-related parts of a control system in respect of their resistance to faults and their subsequent behavior in the fault condition, and which is achieved by the structural arrangement of the parts, fault detection and/or by their reliability. The categories are: B, 1, 2, 3 and 4.

[p367.t1.r6] Term or ab-
breviation: MTTFD | Reference: EN ISO 13849-1 | Description: Mean time to dangerous failure: (Total number of life units) / (Number of dangerous, undetected failures) during a partic- ular measurement interval under stated conditions

breviation: Term or ab- breviation | Reference: Reference | Description: Description
[p368.t1.r2] Term or ab-
breviation: PFDavg | Reference: IEC 61508 | Description: Average probability of dangerous failure on demand, that is, mean unavailability of a safety-related system to perform the specified safety function when a demand occurs
[p368.t1.r3] Term or ab-
breviation: PFH | Reference: IEC 61508 | Description: Average frequency of dangerous failures per hour, that is, average frequency of a dangerous failure of a safety related system to perform the specified safety function over a given period of time
[p368.t1.r4] Term or ab-
breviation: PL | Reference: EN ISO 13849-1 | Description: Performance level. Levels a…e correspond to SIL
[p368.t1.r5] Term or ab-
breviation: Proof test | Reference: IEC 61508, IEC 62061 | Description: Periodic test performed to detect failures in a safety-related system so that, if necessary, a repair can restore the system to an "as new" condition or as close as practical to this con- dition
[p368.t1.r6] Term or ab-
breviation: SC | Reference: IEC 61508 | Description: Systematic capability
[p368.t1.r7] Term or ab-
breviation: SFF | Reference: IEC 61508 | Description: Safe failure fraction (%)
[p368.t1.r8] Term or ab-
breviation: SIL | Reference: IEC 61508 | Description: Safety integrity level (1…3)
[p368.t1.r9] Term or ab-
breviation: STO | Reference: IEC/EN 61800-5-2 | Description: Safe torque off
[p368.t1.r10] Term or ab-
breviation: T1 | Reference: IEC 61508-6 | Description: Proof test interval. T1 is a parameter used to define the probabilistic failure rate (PFH or PFD) for the safety function or subsystem. Performing a proof test at a maximum interval of T1 is required to keep the SIL capability valid. The same interval must be followed to keep the PL capability (EN ISO 13849) valid. See also section Maintenance.
[p368.t1.r11] Term or ab-
breviation: TM | Reference: EN ISO 13849-1 | Description: Mission time: the period of time covering the intended use of the safety function/device. After the mission time elapses, the safety device must be replaced. Note that any TM values given cannot be regarded as a guarantee or warranty.

[p371.b1] Optional I/O extension and adapter modules 367
[p371.b2] 14
[p371.b3] Optional I/O extension and adapter modules
[p371.b4] Contents of this chapter
[p371.b5] This chapter describes how to install and start up the optional CAIO-01, CHDI-01, CMOD-01 and CMOD-02 IO multifunction extension modules and CBAI-01 adapter module. The chapter also contains diagnostics and technical data.
[p371.b6] CAIO-01 bipolar analog I/O adapter module
[p371.b7] ￭Product overview
[p371.b8] The CAIO-01 bipolar analog I/O module expands the inputs and outputs of the drive control unit. It has three bipolar current/voltage inputs and two unipolar current/voltage outputs. The inputs can handle positive and negative signals. The way the drive interprets the negative range of the inputs depends on the parameter settings of the drive. The voltage/current selection of the inputs is done with a parameter.

[p373.b1] Optional I/O extension and adapter modules 369
[p373.b2] ￭Mechanical installation
[p373.b3] Necessary tools
[p373.b4] • Screwdriver and a set of suitable bits.
[p373.b5] Unpacking and examining the delivery
[p373.b6] (step 1) 1. Open the option package. Make sure that the package contains:
[p373.b7] • the option module

[p378.b1] 374 Optional I/O extension and adapter modules
[p378.b2] CBAI-01 bipolar analog IO adapter module
[p378.b3] ￭Product overview
[p378.b4] The CBAI-01 includes two bipolar analog inputs, two unipolar analog outputs, and a switch which can be used to select scaling of the analog output level. The module converts the bipolar analog inputs (-10…+10 V) to respective unipolar analog inputs 0…+10 V which can be connected to the drive control unit. It offers no additional inputs.

[p388.b1] 384 Optional I/O extension and adapter modules
[p388.b2] CMOD-01 multifunction extension module (external 24 V AC/DC and digital I/O)
[p388.b3] ￭Product overview
[p388.b4] The CMOD-01 multifunction extension module (external 24 V AC/DC and digital I/O) expands the outputs of the drive control unit. It has two relay outputs and one transistor output, which can function as a digital or frequency output.
[p388.b5] In addition, the extension module has an external power supply interface, which can be used to power up the drive control unit in case the drive power supply is not on. If you do not need the back-up power supply, you do not have to connect it because the module is powered from the drive control unit by default.
[p388.b6] Note: With CCU-24 control unit, a CMOD-01 module is not necessary for external 24 V AC/DC supply connection. The external supply is connected directly to terminals 40 and 41 on the control unit.

=== page 394 ===
[p394.b1] 390 Optional I/O extension and adapter modules
[p394.b2] CMOD-02 multifunction extension module (external 24 V AC/DC and isolated PTC interface)
[p394.b3] ￭Product overview
[p394.b4] The CMOD-02 multifunction extension module (external 24 V AC/DC and isolated PTC interface) has a motor thermistor connection for supervising the motor temperature and one relay output, which indicates the thermistor status. In case the thermistor overheats, the drive trips on motor overtemperature. If Safe torque off tripping is required, the user must wire the overtemperature indication relay to the certified Safe torque off input of the drive.
[p394.b5] In addition, the extension module has an external power supply interface, which can be used to power up the drive control unit in case the drive power supply is not on. If you do not need the back-up power supply, you do not have to connect it because the module is powered from the drive control unit by default.
[p394.b6] There is reinforced insulation between the motor thermistor connection, the relay output and the drive control unit interface. Thus, you can connect a motor thermistor to the drive through the extension module.
[p394.b7] Note: With CCU-24 control unit, a CMOD-02 module is not necessary for external 24 V AC/DC supply connection. The external supply is connected directly to terminals 40 and 41 on the control unit.

[p395.b10] ￭Mechanical installation
[p395.b11] Necessary tools
[p395.b12] • Screwdriver and a set of suitable bits.
[p395.b13] Unpacking and examining the delivery
[p395.b14] (step 1) 1. Open the option package. Make sure that the package contains:
[p395.b15] • the option module
[p395.b16] • a mounting screw.
[p395.b17] (step 2) 2. Make sure that there are no signs of damage.
[p395.b18] Installing the module
[p395.b19] See section Installing option modules (page 153).
[p395.b20] ￭Electrical installation
[p395.b21] WARNING! Obey the safety instructions of the drive. If you ignore them, injury or death, or damage to the equipment can occur.
=== page 396 ===
[p396.b1] 392 Optional I/O extension and adapter modules
[p396.b2] Stop the drive and do the steps in section Electrical safety precautions (page 22) before you start the work.
[p396.b3] Necessary tools
[p396.b4] • Screwdriver and a set of suitable bits
[p396.b5] Wiring
[p396.b6] Connect the external control cables to the applicable module terminals. Ground the outer shield of the cables 360 degrees under a grounding clamp on the grounding shelf of the control cables.
[p396.b7] WARNING! Do not connect the +24 V AC cable to the control unit ground when the control unit is powered using an external 24 V AC supply.
[p396.b8] ￭Start-up
[p396.b9] Setting the parameters
[p396.b10] (step 1) 1. Power up the drive.
[p396.b11] (step 2) 2. If no warning is shown,
[p396.b12] • make sure that the values of both parameters 15.01 Extension module type and 15.02 Detected extension module are CMOD-02.
[p396.b13] If the warning A7AB Extension I/O configuration failure is shown,
[p396.b14] • make sure that the value of parameter 15.02 is CMOD-02.
[p396.b15] • set the parameter 15.01 value to CMOD-02.
[p396.b16] You can now see the parameters of the extension module in parameter group 15 I/O extension module.
[p396.b17] ￭Diagnostics
[p396.b18] Faults and warning messages
[p396.b19] Warning A7AB Extension I/O configuration failure.
[p396.b20] LEDs
[p396.b21] The extension module has one diagnostic LED.
[p396.t1.r1] TABLE COLUMNS: Color | Description
[p396.t1.r2] Color: Green | Description: The extension module is powered up.
[p396.b22] Description Color
[p396.b23] The extension module is powered up. Green

[p399.b3] Common mode, du/dt and sine filters
[p399.b4] Content of this chapter
[p399.b5] This chapter describes how to select external filters for the drive.
[p399.b6] Common mode filters
[p399.b7] ￭When is a common mode filter needed?
[p399.b8] See section Examining the compatibility of the motor and drive (page 86).
[p399.b9] Common mode filter kits are available from ABB, see the table on page Common mode filter types (page 395). A kit includes three wound cores. For installation instructions of the cores, see the instruction included in the core package.
[p399.b10] ￭Common mode filter types
[p399.b11] IEC ratings at Un = 400 V and 480 V, UL (NEC) ratings at Un = 480 V
[p399.b12] For common mode filters for smaller types, contact your local representative.
